Why Verse 180 Was Revealed: 'And to Allāh Belong the Most Beautiful Names, So Invoke Him by Them!'

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās (At-Tabarī): When the polytheists heard the Prophet ﷺ calling upon *'Yā Allāh, Yā Rahmān'* and falsely claimed he was invoking two deities, Allāh revealed that all the Most Beautiful Names belong to the One True Lord.
tafsirEn.36:12:
Why this verse was revealed — Hadith of Anas & Jābir (Sahīh Muslim #665 & At-Tirmidhī #3226):

📜 Revealed when the Banū Salimah clan wished to move closer to the Prophet's ﷺ Mosque in Madinah; this verse informed them that every step taken from their distant homes is recorded by Allāh.
tafsirEn.36:77:
Why these verses were revealed (Ibn ‘Abbās in Al-Hākim & At-Tabarī):

📜 Revealed when a Quraishi disbeliever crumbled a decayed bone in front of the Prophet ﷺ asking if Allāh could resurrect it; Allāh replied that He who created it the first time brings it back to life by simply saying 'Be!' and it is.
tafsirEn.25:27:
Why this verse was revealed (Ibn ‘Abbās in Abū Dāwūd #4833):

📜 Revealed regarding ‘Uqbah ibn Abī Mu‘ayt, who turned away from the Prophet ﷺ to please his evil companion Ubayy ibn Khalaf, warning of the bitter regret of bad company on Judgment Day.
tafsirEn.25:63:
The Attributes of the Servants of the Most Merciful (‘Ibād ar-Rahmān, v.63–77).

📜 Details the sublime character of true believers: walking in humility, spending nights in prayer, avoiding major sins, and praying for their families.
tafsirEn.67:2:
Testing Who is Best in Deed (Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyād):

📜 Explains that Allāh created death and life to test who is best in deed—meaning the deed that is most sincere for Allāh and most aligned with the Prophetic Sunnah.
tafsirEn.67:15:
True Reliance upon Allāh — Hadith of ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattāb (At-Tirmidhī #2344):

📜 Walking the earth seeking provision while relying upon Allāh like the birds that fly out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening.
tafsirEn.69:40:
How ‘Umar's Heart Opened to Islam (Musnad Ahmad #107):

📜 ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattāb narrated that before his conversion he listened to the Prophet ﷺ reciting Surah Al-Hāqqah by the Ka‘bah; these verses answered every doubt in his mind on the spot and planted faith in his heart.
tafsirEn.19:96:
Divine Love Placed in Hearts — Hadith of Abū Hurayrah (Al-Bukhārī #3209 & Muslim #2637):

📜 When Allāh loves a righteous servant, He calls Jibrīl and the inhabitants of heaven to love him, and places acceptance and affection for him in the hearts of people on earth.
tafsirEn.17:1:
The Night Journey (Al-Isrā') from Makkah to Jerusalem.

📜 When and why this surah was revealed (Hadiths of Anas & Jābir in Al-Bukhārī #3886 & Muslim #162): Revealed in Makkah about one year before the Hijrah following the Year of Sorrow (the passing of Khadījah and Abū Tālib). Allāh honored His Messenger ﷺ by taking him by night on Al-Burāq with Angel Jibrīl from the Sacred Mosque in Makkah to Al-Aqsā Mosque in Jerusalem, where he led the Prophets in prayer before ascending through the heavens.
tafsirEn.17:59:
Why Verse 59 Was Revealed Regarding Makkah's Demand for Physical Miracles.

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās (Musnad Ahmad & At-Tabarī): Revealed when Quraysh asked that Mount As-Safā be turned into gold; Allāh spared them from the immediate destruction that befell Thamūd after rejecting the She-Camel, allowing their descendants to enter Islam.
tafsirEn.17:78:
The Five Daily Prayers & the Witnessed Dawn Recitation — Hadith of Abū Hurayrah (Al-Bukhārī #648 & Muslim #649):

📜 Establishes the prayer times from the sun's decline to nightfall and highlights the Dawn prayer (Fajr), which is witnessed by both the angels of the night and the angels of the day.
tafsirEn.17:85:
When and Why Verse 85 Was Revealed: 'And They Ask You About the Soul (Ar-Rūh)!'

📜 Hadith of ‘Abdullāh ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #125 & Muslim #2794): While the Prophet ﷺ was walking in Madinah with Ibn Mas‘ūd, Jewish rabbis asked him about the Soul (*Ar-Rūh*), and Allāh revealed: 'Say: The Soul is of the affair of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little!'
tafsirEn.17:110:
When and Why Verse 110 Was Revealed: The Middle Path in Voice During Prayer in Makkah.

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4722 & Muslim #446): Revealed in Makkah when the polytheists used to revile the Quran whenever they heard the Prophet ﷺ recite aloud in prayer, instructing him to seek a moderate tone between loudness and whispering.
tafsirEn.10:1:
Why Surah Yūnus was revealed in Makkah (Ibn ‘Abbās):

📜 Revealed when the leaders of Quraysh marveled that Allāh had chosen Muhammad ﷺ as a Messenger from among mankind to warn people and bring glad tidings to the believers.
tafsirEn.10:25:
The Abode of Peace & the Ultimate Reward — Hadith of Suhayb Ar-Rūmī (Sahīh Muslim #181):

📜 The Prophet ﷺ explained that in verse 26, 'the best reward' (Al-Husnā) is Paradise and 'the addition' (Az-Ziyādah) is beholding the noble Countenance of Allāh.
tafsirEn.10:90:
Pharaoh's Preserved Body vs. the Repentance of the People of Yūnus (v.90–98):

📜 Contrasts Pharaoh—whose deathbed confession was rejected as he drowned and whose body was preserved as a lasting sign—with the people of Prophet Yūnus in Nineveh, whose sincere collective repentance lifted the punishment before it struck.
tafsirEn.11:1:
When and why Surah Hūd was revealed — Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās (At-Tirmidhī #3297):

📜 Revealed in Makkah during intense persecution after the Year of Sorrow to strengthen the hearts of the Prophet ﷺ and the believers through the accounts of the earlier Prophets.
tafsirEn.11:112:
Steadfastness & Why Verse 114 Was Revealed — Hadith of Ibn Mas‘ūd (Al-Bukhārī #526 & Muslim #2763):

📜 Commands unwavering uprightness (v.112), followed by verse 114 revealed regarding a companion who came repentant after a minor slip and prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, announcing that regular prayers at both ends of the day and early night wipe away sins.
tafsirEn.12:1:
Why and when Surah Yūsuf was revealed in Makkah (Sa‘d ibn Abī Waqqās & Ibn ‘Abbās):

📜 Revealed all at once in Makkah both to comfort the persecuted believers and to answer Quraishi inquiries about how Jacob's family entered Egypt. Prophet Yūsuf's journey—betrayed by his brothers, exiled, raised to authority, and ultimately forgiving his brothers—foreshadowed Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ own journey with his Quraishi kindred culminating in his forgiveness at the Conquest of Makkah (v.92).
tafsirEn.15:9:
Why Verse 9 Was Revealed — The Divine Preservation of the Quran:

📜 Revealed in response to Makkan mockers who thought the message would fade away, proclaiming Allāh's eternal guarantee to guard the Quran from any corruption.
tafsirEn.15:87:
The Seven Oft-Repeated Verses (Al-Fātihah) — Hadith of Abū Sa‘īd & Abū Hurayrah (Al-Bukhārī #4474 & #4703):

📜 The Prophet ﷺ explained that the 'Seven Oft-Repeated Verses' gifted to him in this verse are Surah Al-Fātihah, recited in every unit of prayer.
tafsirEn.15:94:
When Public Preaching Began in Makkah (Ibn ‘Abbās & Sa‘īd ibn Jubayr):

📜 Revealed after three years of private invitation in Makkah to command open proclamation of the Truth, guaranteeing divine protection against the five chief mockers of Quraysh (v.95) and prescribing praise, prostration, and constant worship to heal tightness of the chest (v.97–99).
tafsirEn.6:1:
When and how Surah Al-An‘ām was revealed all at once in Makkah.

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās, Jābir & Anas (Al-Hākim, At-Tabarī & Al-Bayhaqī): Unlike most long surahs revealed in stages, Surah Al-An‘ām descended all at once at night in Makkah, escorted by seventy thousand angels glorifying Allāh, to dismantle every pillar of Makkan polytheism and their superstitions regarding livestock and idol offerings.
tafsirEn.6:33:
Why this verse was revealed to console the Prophet ﷺ — Hadith of ‘Alī & Ibn ‘Abbās (At-Tirmidhī #3064):

📜 Revealed after Abū Jahl told the Prophet ﷺ that Quraysh did not consider him personally a liar (since they knew his lifelong honesty), yet rejected the message he brought; Allāh consoled His Messenger ﷺ affirming that the wrongdoers are in truth knowingly denying the signs of Allāh.
tafsirEn.6:52:
When and Why Verse 52 Was Revealed: 'And Do Not Send Away Those Who Call Upon Their Lord Morning and Evening!'

📜 Hadith of Sa‘d ibn Abī Waqqās & Ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Muslim #2413): Revealed when arrogant chiefs of Quraysh asked the Prophet ﷺ to dismiss poor believers (such as Bilāl, ‘Ammār, Suhayb, Khabbāb, and Ibn Mas‘ūd) from his gathering; Allāh forbade ever sending away sincere believers who seek His Face.
tafsirEn.6:82:
How the Prophet ﷺ Explained 'Injustice (Az-Zulm)' in Verse 82 Through Luqmān's Words.

📜 Hadith of ‘Abdullāh ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3360 & Muslim #124): When this verse was revealed, the companions were distressed and asked who among them had never wronged himself; the Prophet ﷺ explained that *Zulm* here means *Shirk* (polytheism), citing Surah 31:13.
tafsirEn.6:151:
The Ten Universal Moral Commandments Revealed in Makkah (v.151–153 — Ibn Mas‘ūd):

📜 Ibn Mas‘ūd called these three verses the moral testament sealed by the Prophet ﷺ: forbidding polytheism, enjoining kindness to parents, protecting children's lives, shunning open and secret indecencies, upholding the sanctity of life, safeguarding the orphan's wealth, maintaining justice in measure and speech, and following Allāh's Straight Path.
tafsirEn.37:1:
Why Surah As-Sāffāt was revealed — Hadith of Jābir ibn Samurah (Sahīh Muslim #430):

📜 Allāh swears by the angels standing in ranks in the heavens—after whom the Prophet ﷺ instructed believers to straighten their rows in prayer—to proclaim Divine Oneness (v.4) and refute Quraishi claims that angels were Allāh's daughters (v.149–153).
tafsirEn.37:62:
Why the verses on the Tree of Zaqqūm were revealed (Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah):

📜 Revealed when Abū Jahl mocked the mention of a tree growing at the bottom of Hellfire, claiming fire burns trees; Allāh declared that Zaqqūm was made a trial for the wrongdoers.
tafsirEn.37:102:
Why the Sacrifice of Ibrāhīm and Ismā‘īl was recounted to Makkah (v.100–111):

📜 Reminded Quraysh—who took pride in descending from Ibrāhīm and Ismā‘īl while worshipping idols—of their forefathers' total submission to the One True God.
tafsirEn.31:1:
Why Surah Luqmān was revealed in Makkah:

📜 Revealed when the Makkans asked about the wisdom of Luqmān, showing that the foundation of all true wisdom begins with pure monotheism and rejecting polytheism.
tafsirEn.31:6:
Why this verse was revealed regarding 'Idle Tales' (Ibn ‘Abbās & Ibn Mas‘ūd):

📜 Revealed in Makkah regarding An-Nadr ibn Al-Hārith, who purchased Persian legends and singing girls to distract people in Makkah from listening to the Quran.
tafsirEn.31:14:
When and why the verses on parents were revealed — Hadith of Sa‘d ibn Abī Waqqās (Sahīh Muslim #2412 & At-Tirmidhī #3189):

📜 Revealed when Sa‘d's mother vowed neither to eat nor drink until death unless he renounced Islam; Allāh commanded never to obey parents in polytheism while continuing to treat them with kindness and respect in this world.
tafsirEn.31:34:
Why the final verse on the Five Keys of the Unseen was revealed — Hadith of Ibn ‘Umar & Abū Hurayrah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #50 & #4778):

📜 Revealed when a man asked the Prophet ﷺ about the timing of the Hour, rainfall, and what his pregnant wife would bear; Allāh revealed the five keys of the Unseen known exclusively to Him.
tafsirEn.34:15:
Why the Story of Saba' was revealed to Quraysh (v.15–19 — At-Tirmidhī #3222):

📜 Revealed as a direct warning to the merchants of Makkah, showing how the prosperous kingdom of Saba' in Yemen lost its two lush gardens through the flood of the ‘Arim dam when they met Allāh's blessings with ingratitude.
tafsirEn.34:23:
Intercession by Allāh's Permission & the Awe of the Angels — Hadith of Abū Hurayrah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4800):

📜 Refutes the idolaters' belief in independent intercession, describing how even the mighty angels beat their wings in awe when Allāh speaks His decree in the heavens.
tafsirEn.39:3:
Why the opening of Az-Zumar was revealed (Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah):

📜 Revealed to refute the Quraishi polytheists who admitted Allāh is the Creator yet claimed: 'We only worship these idols so that they may bring us nearer to Allāh!', establishing that pure devotion belongs to Allāh alone.
tafsirEn.39:53:
Context of Verse 53: The Verse of Ultimate Hope and Universal Forgiveness for the Repentant.

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4810 & Muslim #122): Revealed to assure those who feared their past sins were beyond pardon that Allāh forgives all sins entirely for whoever turns back to Him in sincere repentance and never despairs of His mercy.
tafsirEn.40:1:
Why Surah Ghāfir was revealed in Makkah (v.1–5):

📜 First of the seven Hā-Mīm surahs, revealed in Makkah when Quraishi leaders plotted against the Prophet ﷺ, opening with Allāh's attributes as Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, and Severe in punishment.
tafsirEn.40:28:
The Believer from Pharaoh's Family & Abū Bakr As-Siddīq Defending the Prophet ﷺ — Hadith of ‘Urwah & ‘Abdullāh ibn ‘Amr (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3678, #3856 & #4815):

📜 When ‘Uqbah ibn Abī Mu‘ayt twisted his garment around the Prophet's ﷺ neck while he was praying at the Ka‘bah, Abū Bakr As-Siddīq rushed forward, pushed the attacker away, and cried out with the exact words of this verse: 'Would you kill a man simply because he says: My Lord is Allāh, while he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?'
tafsirEn.40:46:
Proof of the Punishment of the Grave (Barzakh) — Hadith of Ibn ‘Umar (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #1379 & Muslim #2866):

📜 Just as Pharaoh's people are exposed to the Fire morning and evening before the Hour is established, the Prophet ﷺ taught that every deceased person is shown their future place morning and evening in the grave until Resurrection Day.
tafsirEn.40:60:
'Call upon Me; I will respond to you!' — Hadith of An-Nu‘mān ibn Bashīr (At-Tirmidhī #3247 & Abū Dāwūd #1479):

📜 Explaining this verse, the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'Supplication (Ad-Du‘ā') is worship itself!'
tafsirEn.41:1:
When and why the opening of Surah Fussilat was revealed (v.1–13 — Account of ‘Utbah ibn Rabī‘ah):

📜 When Quraysh sent their eloquent spokesman ‘Utbah ibn Rabī‘ah to offer the Prophet ﷺ wealth or kingship to stop preaching, the Prophet ﷺ recited to him the opening of Surah Fussilat up to verse 13; overwhelmed by its majesty, ‘Utbah placed his hand over the Prophet's ﷺ mouth begging him by kinship to stop lest the punishment fall immediately, and returned to tell Quraysh that what he heard was neither poetry, sorcery, nor divination.
tafsirEn.41:22:
Context of Verses 22–24: The Dispute of Three Men Near the Ka‘bah Regarding Allāh's All-Encompassing Hearing.

📜 Hadith of ‘Abdullāh ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4817 & Muslim #2775): Revealed when three men near the Ka‘bah wondered whether Allāh heard their secret whispers; Allāh declared that nothing is hidden from Him and that a person's own hearing, sight, and skin will bear witness on Judgment Day.
tafsirEn.41:30:
Angels Descending upon the Steadfast — Hadith of Sufyān ibn ‘Abdillāh (Sahīh Muslim #38):

📜 When asked for a comprehensive word on Islam, the Prophet ﷺ replied with the essence of this verse: 'Say: I believe in Allāh, and then remain upright (Istaqim)!'
tafsirEn.42:13:
Why Surah Ash-Shūrā was revealed: The Unity of All Prophets' Religion:

📜 Revealed in Makkah affirming that the religion ordained for Muhammad ﷺ is the exact same pure monotheism ordained for Nūh, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā, and ‘Īsā.
tafsirEn.42:23:
Why this verse on the Ties of Kinship was revealed — Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4818):

📜 Ibn ‘Abbās explained that the Prophet ﷺ had blood ties to every sub-clan of Quraysh; this verse was revealed telling them: 'I ask no worldly wage from you, except that you honor the ties of kinship between us by not harming me as I convey Allāh's message!'
tafsirEn.42:51:
Why this verse was revealed: The Three Modes of Divine Revelation (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #2):

📜 Revealed defining the three ways Allāh communicates with a prophet: direct inspiration, speaking from behind a veil (as with Mūsā and Muhammad ﷺ during the Ascension), or sending an angelic Messenger (Jibrīl).
tafsirEn.43:31:
Why these verses were revealed (v.31–32 — Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah):

📜 Revealed when Al-Walīd ibn Al-Mughīrah and Quraishi notables objected: 'Why was this Quran not sent down to a wealthy chief of Makkah or Tā'if?'; Allāh answered: 'Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?'
tafsirEn.43:57:
Why the verses on ‘Īsā (Jesus) were revealed (v.57–60 — Ibn ‘Abbās in Ahmad #1920):

📜 Revealed when the polytheist Ibn Az-Ziba‘rā argued out of contentiousness that since Christians worship Jesus, Jesus would fall under verse 21:98; Allāh exposed their sophistry, affirming that Jesus was a righteous servant blessed by Allāh who never called people to worship him.
tafsirEn.44:1:
Revelation of the Quran on the Blessed Night (Laylat al-Qadr, v.1–6 — Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah):

📜 Allāh swears by the Clear Book that He sent it down on the blessed Night of Decree in Ramadān.
tafsirEn.44:10:
When and why the verses of the Smoke (Ad-Dukhān) and the Great Assault of Badr were revealed — Hadith of Ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4821, #4824 & Sahīh Muslim #2798):

📜 When Quraysh persisted in persecuting the believers in Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ prayed for seven years of drought like the years of Yūsuf until they saw a haze like smoke (Ad-Dukhān) between them and the sky from severe hunger (v.10). After Abū Sufyān pleaded with the Prophet ﷺ to pray for relief, the drought was lifted, yet they returned to rebellion until Allāh struck them with the 'Greatest Assault' (v.16) at the Battle of Badr.
tafsirEn.45:1:
Why Surah Al-Jāthiyah was revealed in Makkah (v.1–6):

📜 Revealed in Makkah calling upon Quraysh to reflect on Allāh's signs in the heavens, earth, and winds, and warning of the Day when every nation will be seen kneeling (Jāthiyah, v.28) before Allāh's Judgment.
tafsirEn.45:23:
Why these verses were revealed against attributing life and death to 'Time' (Ad-Dahr, v.23–24) — Hadith Qudsī of Abū Hurayrah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4826 & Muslim #2246):

📜 Revealed refuting the pre-Islamic materialists who denied the Resurrection saying: 'Nothing destroys us except Time (Ad-Dahr)!' Commenting on this verse, the Prophet ﷺ narrated that Allāh said: 'The son of Adam offends Me by cursing Time, whereas I am the Master of Time; in My Hand is the command, and I alternate the night and the day!'
tafsirEn.46:15:
Context of Verse 15: Filial Piety and the Supplication at Age Forty (Exemplified by Abū Bakr As-Siddīq).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & ‘Alī (At-Tabarī): Highlights the mother's hardship in pregnancy and weaning and the believer's prayer at forty for gratitude and righteous offspring—fulfilled completely in **Abū Bakr As-Siddīq**, whose parents, children, and grandchildren all embraced Islam.
tafsirEn.46:21:
Why the Story of Hūd in the Sand Dunes (Al-Ahqāf) was revealed — Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4829 & Muslim #899):

📜 Recounts how the people of ‘Ād mistook the approaching cloud of punishment for rain. ‘Ā'ishah narrated that whenever the Prophet ﷺ saw a strong wind or dark cloud, concern showed on his face remembering what the people of ‘Ād said, until rain fell and he felt relieved.
tafsirEn.46:29:
When and why the verses on the Jinn listening to the Quran were revealed (v.29–32 — Sahīh Muslim #450 & At-Tirmidhī #3258):

📜 Revealed after the Prophet's ﷺ difficult return from Tā'if: at Wādī Nakhlah during the night prayer, Allāh directed a group of jinn to listen to his recitation, who told one another 'Listen in silence!' and returned as warners to their people.
tafsirEn.51:1:
The Four Cosmic Oaths Affirming the Resurrection (v.1–6 — Exegesis of ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib):

📜 ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib explained that Allāh swears by the scattering winds (v.1), rain-bearing clouds (v.2), smoothly sailing ships (v.3), and angels distributing decrees (v.4) that the promised Resurrection and Judgment are true.
tafsirEn.51:56:
The Supreme Purpose of Creation (v.56–58 — ‘Alī & Ibn ‘Abbās):

📜 'And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me (to know My Oneness and obey Me)', while Allāh alone is the All-Provider (Ar-Razzāq), Possessor of Unshakeable Strength.
tafsirEn.18:1:
When and why Surah Al-Kahf was revealed in Makkah — The Three Questions (Ibn ‘Abbās & Sahīh Muslim #809):

📜 Revealed when Quraysh sent envoys to the rabbis in Madinah, who instructed them to test the Prophet ﷺ with three questions: the Youths of the Cave (v.9–26), the traveler who reached the east and west of the earth (Dhū al-Qarnayn, v.83–98), and the Spirit (Ar-Rūh). In Sahīh Muslim (#809), the Prophet ﷺ taught that whoever memorizes the first ten verses of Surah Al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Antichrist (Ad-Dajjāl).
tafsirEn.18:28:
When and Why Verse 28 Was Revealed: 'And Keep Yourself Patient with Those Who Call Upon Their Lord Morning and Evening!'

📜 Hadith of Sa‘d ibn Abī Waqqās & Salmān (Sahīh Muslim #2413 & Ibn Mājah #4127): Revealed when proud tribal chiefs asked the Prophet ﷺ to hold a separate gathering away from the poor companions (like Salmān, Bilāl, and Suhayb); the Prophet ﷺ praised Allāh and sat closely among the humble believers.
tafsirEn.18:60:
Why the Story of Mūsā and Al-Khidr was revealed (v.60–82 — Hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka‘b in Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #122 & Muslim #2380):

📜 Revealed showing how Mūsā traveled to the junction of the two seas to learn from Al-Khidr the hidden wisdom behind Allāh's decrees (the damaged boat saved from a tyrant king, the boy, and the wall rebuilt to protect the treasure of two orphans).
tafsirEn.18:109:
Why the Final Verses on Allāh's Infinite Words were revealed (v.109–110 — Al-Hākim & At-Tabarī):

📜 Revealed to show that all knowledge granted to creation is finite beside Allāh's infinite Knowledge: if the sea were ink for the Words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the Words of my Lord were exhausted.
tafsirEn.16:1:
Why the opening of Surah An-Nahl (The Surah of Blessings) was revealed (Ibn ‘Abbās):

📜 Revealed when the Makkan polytheists mockingly demanded that the promised punishment be hastened upon them.
tafsirEn.16:68:
Divine Inspiration to the Bee & Healing in Honey (v.68–69 — Hadith of Abū Sa‘īd in Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #5684 & Muslim #2217):

📜 When a man's brother suffered from a stomach ailment, the Prophet ﷺ instructed him repeatedly to give him honey, saying: 'Allāh has spoken the truth, and your brother's stomach has lied; give him honey to drink!'—whereupon he was completely cured.
tafsirEn.16:103:
Why Verse 103 Was Revealed Refuting the Claim of a Human Teacher (At-Tabarī):

📜 Revealed when Quraysh claimed that a non-Arab Christian blacksmith in Makkah taught the Prophet ﷺ; Allāh refuted them pointing out that the man's tongue was foreign while this Quran is in pure, inimitable Arabic.
tafsirEn.16:106:
When and Why Verse 106 Was Revealed Regarding One Forced Under Torture While His Heart Is Tranquil in Faith (‘Ammār ibn Yāsir).

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah (Al-Hākim, Al-Bayhaqī & At-Tabarī): Revealed regarding **‘Ammār ibn Yāsir** when the polytheists tortured him after martyring his parents Yāsir and Summayyah until he uttered words under duress while his heart remained completely firm and serene in faith.
tafsirEn.16:126:
When and Why Verses 126–128 Were Revealed Calling for Patience After the Martyrdom of Hamzah at Uhud.

📜 Hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka‘b & Abū Hurayrah (At-Tirmidhī #3129 & Al-Hākim): Revealed on the Day of Uhud when the Prophet ﷺ was grieved by the mutilation of his uncle **Hamzah**; Allāh called him to patience, whereupon he expiated his oath and forgave Quraysh upon the Conquest of Makkah.
tafsirEn.71:1:
Historical Context of Surah Nūh in Makkah (v.1–20):

📜 Revealed all at once in Makkah to strengthen the Prophet ﷺ against the stubbornness of Quraysh, recounting Prophet Nūh's 950-year call to monotheism and how seeking Allāh's forgiveness (Istighfār, v.10–12) brings abundant rain, blessings in wealth and children, and salvation.
tafsirEn.71:21:
Origin of the Five Idols of Nūh's People (v.21–24 — Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās in Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4920):

📜 Ibn ‘Abbās explained that Wadd, Suwā‘, Yaghūth, Ya‘ūq, and Nasr were originally five righteous men whose memorial statues were later worshipped by succeeding generations at Satan's instigation.
tafsirEn.14:1:
Why Surah Ibrāhīm Was Revealed in Makkah (v.1–7):

📜 Revealed to show the mission of the Book in bringing humanity out of darkness into the Light of Monotheism, and establishing the spiritual law that gratitude to Allāh increases His blessings (v.7).
tafsirEn.14:24:
Parable of the Goodly Tree & Steadfastness in the Grave (v.24–27 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4698 & #1369):

📜 The Prophet ﷺ identified the deeply rooted tree representing sincere faith as the date palm, and explained that verse 27 refers to Allāh keeping the believer firm both in this world and when questioned by the two angels in the grave.
tafsirEn.14:28:
Reason for Revelation Regarding the Ungrateful Leaders of Quraysh (v.28–30 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3977 & #4700):

📜 ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattāb and Ibn ‘Abbās explained that this passage refers to the disbelieving chiefs of Quraysh who met Allāh's blessing of the Sanctuary and the Prophet's ﷺ mission with hostility, leading their followers to defeat at Badr.
tafsirEn.21:1:
Context of Surah Al-Anbiyā' Awakening the Heedless in Makkah (v.1–7):

📜 Revealed as a wake-up call to the mockers of Makkah as the Day of Account approaches, reminding them that all Messengers before Muhammad ﷺ were likewise human beings inspired by Allāh.
tafsirEn.21:30:
Cosmic Signs: Separation of the Heavens and Earth & Water as the Basis of Life (v.30–33 — Ibn ‘Abbās):

📜 Calls disbelievers to reflect on how the heavens and earth formed a single joined entity before Allāh separated them, and how every living creature was made from water.
tafsirEn.21:98:
Why Verses 98–101 Were Revealed (Ibn ‘Abbās):

📜 Clarifies against the contentious objection of Ibn Az-Ziba‘rā that Allāh's righteous servants and Prophets (such as Jesus) are completely exempt from the warning addressed to idols.
tafsirEn.23:1:
Revelation of the Ten Verses of the Inheritors of Al-Firdaws (v.1–11 — At-Tirmidhī #3173):

📜 ‘Umar narrated that when these opening ten verses descended, the Prophet ﷺ announced that whoever embodies their virtues—humility in prayer, shunning vain talk, giving Zakāt, guarding chastity, and keeping trusts—will inherit the highest Paradise (Al-Firdaws).
tafsirEn.23:60:
The Humble Fear of the Righteous — Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah (At-Tirmidhī #3175):

📜 The Prophet ﷺ explained to ‘Ā'ishah that this verse describes believers who fast, pray, and give charity while humbly fearing that their deeds may fall short of acceptance.
tafsirEn.32:1:
Virtue of Surah As-Sajdah in the Prophet's ﷺ Recitation (v.1–15 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #891):

📜 Recited regularly by the Prophet ﷺ at the Friday dawn prayer and before sleep.
tafsirEn.32:16:
Context of Verses 16–18: Night Devotion of the Believers and the Contrast Between the Believer and the Defiant.

📜 Account of Anas, Mu‘ādh & Ibn ‘Abbās (Abū Dāwūd #1321 & At-Tabarī): Praises the companions who rose from their beds at night to pray to their Lord in fear and hope, and affirms that the sincere believer is never equal to the rebellious transgressor.
tafsirEn.32:18:
Why Verses 18–20 Were Revealed: The Believer vs. the Defiant Rebel (Ibn ‘Abbās):

📜 Revealed contrasting the destiny of the sincere believer with that of the arrogant transgressor: they are never equal before Allāh.
tafsirEn.52:1:
The Five Solemn Oaths Affirming the Day of Judgment (v.1–8 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3207):

📜 Swears by Mount Sinai, the inscribed Scripture, the Much-Frequented House in the seventh heaven (Al-Bayt al-Ma‘mūr, entered daily by 70,000 angels), the raised canopy of the sky, and the surging sea that Allāh's judgment will surely come to pass.
tafsirEn.52:35:
When Jubayr ibn Mut‘im Heard the Prophet ﷺ Recite Verses 35–37 (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4854 & Muslim #463):

📜 Coming to Madinah before his conversion to ransom captives after Badr, Jubayr ibn Mut‘im heard the Prophet ﷺ recite Surah At-Tūr in the Maghrib prayer; upon hearing these three verses questioning how anyone could exist without a Creator, his heart nearly took flight and faith first entered his soul.
tafsirEn.29:1:
Why the Opening of Surah Al-‘Ankabūt Was Revealed: The Law of Testing Faith (v.1–3):

📜 Revealed to comfort and strengthen the persecuted companions in Makkah, establishing that trials distinguish true believers from the insincere.
tafsirEn.29:8:
Context of Verse 8: Sa‘d ibn Abī Waqqās's Kindness to His Mother Alongside Firmness in Faith.

📜 Hadith of Sa‘d ibn Abī Waqqās (Sahīh Muslim #1748 & At-Tirmidhī #3189): Revealed when Sa‘d's mother vowed to abstain from food and drink until he abandoned Islam; Allāh commanded exemplary kindness to parents in worldly matters while forbidding obedience to anyone in associating partners with Allāh.
tafsirEn.29:41:
The Parable of the Spider's Web Against Idolatry:

📜 Likens reliance upon false deities beside Allāh to the frailest of all homes—the spider's web.
tafsirEn.30:1:
When and Why the Prophecy of the Byzantine Victory Was Revealed (v.1–6 — At-Tirmidhī #3192 & #3193):

📜 Revealed in Makkah when the Persian Empire defeated the Byzantines (People of the Book) and the Makkan polytheists gloated over the Muslims; Allāh foretold that the defeated Byzantines would triumph within three to nine years (Bid‘i sinīn), a prophecy publicly championed by Abū Bakr As-Siddīq and fulfilled concurrently with the Muslims' own triumph.
tafsirEn.2:1:
Historical Context of Surah Al-Baqarah in Madinah & Its Virtues (Sahīh Muslim #780 & #804):

📜 As the first major surah revealed in Madinah after the Hijrah, its revelation spanned several years to establish the foundations of the Muslim community, its acts of worship, and its ethical and legal framework. The Prophet ﷺ taught that Satan flees from any home in which Surah Al-Baqarah is recited.
tafsirEn.2:142:
The Change of the Qiblah Toward the Ka‘bah (v.142–144).

📜 Revealed in Madinah when the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to turn his face toward the Sacred Mosque in Makkah.
tafsirEn.2:183:
The Prescription of Fasting in Ramadān (v.183–187).

📜 Ordained in Year 2 AH so that believers may attain piety and gratitude.
tafsirEn.2:255:
Āyat al-Kursī (The Verse of the Throne).

📜 The greatest verse of the Quran encompassing Allāh's absolute Oneness and eternal sustaining power.
tafsirEn.2:285:
The Concluding Verses of Al-Baqarah (v.285–286).

📜 Gifted during the Night Ascension, affirming that Allāh never burdens a soul beyond its capacity.
tafsirEn.8:1:
The Spoils of War after Badr (v.1–4).

📜 Revealed after the Battle of Badr to assign the ruling of spoils to Allāh and His Messenger ﷺ.
tafsirEn.8:9:
When and Why Verses 9–10 Were Revealed: The Prophet's ﷺ Supplication at Badr and the Thousand Angels.

📜 Hadith of ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattāb & Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Muslim #1763 & Al-Bukhārī #3953): Revealed on the Day of Badr when the Prophet ﷺ raised his hands in fervent supplication until his cloak fell from his shoulders, and Allāh answered immediately with a thousand angels in succession.
tafsirEn.8:33:
Why Verse 33 Was Revealed: The Two Safeguards Against Collective Punishment.

📜 Hadith of Anas ibn Mālik & Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4648 & Muslim #2796): Revealed after Abū Jahl arrogantly asked for stones to rain from the sky (v.32), declaring that Allāh would not punish them collectively while the Prophet ﷺ was among them nor while believers seek forgiveness (*Istighfār*).
tafsirEn.3:1:
When and Why the Opening of Surah Āl ‘Imrān Was Revealed (v.1–83 — Delegation of Najrān):

📜 The first eighty-some verses were revealed in Madinah when the Christian delegation of Najrān came to debate with the Prophet ﷺ, clarifying pure Monotheism, the distinction between clear foundational verses and allegorical ones (v.7), and the true history of Maryam and the miraculous birth of ‘Īsā (Jesus), whose creation without a father is likened to Adam's creation from dust (v.59).
tafsirEn.3:121:
The Lessons of the Battle of Uhud (v.121–179).

📜 Revealed following the test of Uhud to console the believers and honor the martyrs.
tafsirEn.3:169:
When and Why Verses 169–171 Were Revealed: The Eternal Life of the Martyrs Near Their Lord.

📜 Hadith of Jābir ibn ‘Abdillāh & Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Muslim #1887 & Abū Dāwūd #2520): Revealed regarding the martyrs of Badr and Uhud (including Jābir's father, ‘Abdullāh ibn ‘Amr ibn Harām): their souls live inside green birds that roam freely through Paradise and rest in golden lanterns suspended beneath the Throne of Allāh.
tafsirEn.3:190:
Revelation of the Final Ten Verses of Āl ‘Imrān (v.190–200 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4569 & Muslim #256):

📜 Revealed late at night calling believers to ponder the creation of the heavens and earth; the Prophet ﷺ wept in night prayer while reciting them and urged everyone who reads them to reflect deeply upon their meaning.
tafsirEn.33:4:
Context of Verses 4–5: Abolishing Pre-Islamic Zihār and Restoring True Lineage (Zayd ibn Hārithah).

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Umar (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4782 & Muslim #2425): Prior to this verse, Zayd ibn Hārithah was called 'Zayd son of Muhammad' according to pre-Islamic adoptive custom; Allāh commanded that children be attributed to their biological fathers in justice while preserving brotherhood in faith.
tafsirEn.33:9:
The Battle of the Trench / Al-Ahzāb (v.9–27).

📜 Recounts how Allāh aided the believers against the confederate armies with a piercing wind and unseen angels.
tafsirEn.33:35:
Context of Verse 35: Equal Spiritual Honor of Believing Men and Believing Women (Umm Salamah's Question).

📜 Hadith of Umm Salamah (At-Tirmidhī #3211 & Musnad Ahmad): When Umm Salamah asked why men were often mentioned explicitly in accounts of migration and striving, Allāh revealed this comprehensive verse naming believing men and women side by side across ten noble virtues rewarded with forgiveness and a vast reward.
tafsirEn.33:56:
Command to Send Blessings and Peace upon the Prophet ﷺ (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4797 & Muslim #406):

📜 Upon the revelation of this verse, the companions asked how to send blessings upon him, and the Prophet ﷺ taught them the Ibrāhīmiyyah salutation recited in every prayer.
tafsirEn.60:1:
Context of Verses 1–4: The Letter of Hātib ibn Abī Balta‘ah Before the Conquest of Makkah.

📜 Hadith of ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3007, #4890 & Muslim #2494): Revealed when Hātib sent a letter seeking to protect his vulnerable relatives in Makkah; the Prophet ﷺ retrieved the letter, accepted Hātib's sincere excuse as a veteran of Badr, and received the opening of this surah.
tafsirEn.60:10:
Context of Verse 10: Protecting Believing Women Who Emigrated to Madinah (Umm Kulthūm bint ‘Uqbah).

📜 Hadith of Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #2712 & #4891): Revealed after Al-Hudaybiyah when Umm Kulthūm bint ‘Uqbah escaped Makkah on foot to join Madinah, forbidding returning believing women to the polytheists.
tafsirEn.4:1:
When and Why Surah An-Nisā' Was Revealed in Madinah (v.1–6 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4574 & Muslim #3018):

📜 Revealed in Madinah after the Battle of Uhud—which left many widows and orphans in the Muslim community—opening with a call to revere Allāh who created humanity from a single soul (Adam) and to safeguard kinship ties and the rights and wealth of orphans and women.
tafsirEn.4:7:
Inheritance Rights for Women and Children (v.7–11).

📜 Abolished pre-Islamic injustice by guaranteeing fixed, obligatory shares of inheritance for women and children.
tafsirEn.4:41:
The Verse That Brought Tears to the Prophet's ﷺ Eyes — Hadith of Ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4582 & Muslim #800):

📜 Ibn Mas‘ūd narrated that the Prophet ﷺ asked him to recite the Quran to him; he recited Surah An-Nisā' until reaching verse 41: 'So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you (O Muhammad) as a witness over these?' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'That is enough for now,' and Ibn Mas‘ūd saw his eyes overflowing with tears.
tafsirEn.4:58:
When and Why Verse 58 Was Revealed: 'Indeed, Allāh Commands You to Render Trusts to Whom They Are Due!'

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid (At-Tabarī & Ibn Hishām): On the day of the Conquest of Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ took the key of the Ka‘bah from ‘Uthmān ibn Talhah to purify the Sanctuary; as he came out reciting this newly revealed verse, he returned the key of the Ka‘bah to ‘Uthmān ibn Talhah and his descendants forever.
tafsirEn.4:176:
The Final Verse Revealed on Inheritance (Āyat al-Kalālah) During Jābir's Illness.

📜 Hadith of Jābir ibn ‘Abdillāh & Al-Barā' (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4605, #194 & Muslim #1616): When Jābir fell gravely ill and asked the Prophet ﷺ how his estate should be divided among his sisters since he had no ascendants or descendants (*Kalālah*), Allāh revealed this concluding verse of Surah An-Nisā'.
tafsirEn.99:1:
The Final Earthquake & the Testimony of the Earth (v.1–5 — Hadith of Abū Hurayrah in At-Tirmidhī #2429):

📜 Reciting verse 4 ('That Day, it will report its news'), the Prophet ﷺ explained that the earth's news is its testimony for or against every human being regarding every deed done upon its surface.
tafsirEn.99:7:
The All-Encompassing Verses on an Atom's Weight of Good or Evil (v.7–8 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3646 & Muslim #987):

📜 Revealed when some people thought small charities brought no reward and minor sins brought no accountability; the Prophet ﷺ called these two verses the unique, all-comprehensive verses (Al-Fādhah Al-Jāmi‘ah).
tafsirEn.57:1:
Universal Glorification of Allāh & Spending in His Cause (v.1–11):

📜 Revealed in Madinah urging believers to spend for Allāh's cause and highlighting in verse 10 the excellence of those who spent and strove before the Victory, while promising Paradise to both groups of companions.
tafsirEn.57:12:
The Light of Believing Men and Women on the Bridge (As-Sirāt, v.12–15):

📜 Depicts the Day when believers will see their light shining ahead of them and to their right in proportion to their faith and deeds.
tafsirEn.57:16:
When and Why Verse 16 Was Revealed Awakening Humble Hearts — Statement of Ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Muslim #3027):

📜 Ibn Mas‘ūd stated that only four years separated their acceptance of Islam and the revelation of this gentle admonition calling believers' hearts to humble themselves at the remembrance of Allāh and the Truth.
tafsirEn.47:1:
Why Surah Muhammad Was Revealed in Madinah Before Badr (v.1–7):

📜 Revealed early in Madinah as Quraysh prepared war against the believers, promising that Allāh expiates the sins of those who believe in what was revealed to Muhammad ﷺ (v.2) and establishing the divine law: 'If you support the cause of Allāh, He will support you and make your foothold firm!' (v.7).
tafsirEn.47:24:
The Call to Deep Reflection upon the Quran (At-Tadabbur):

📜 'Then do they not reflect upon the Quran, or are there locks upon their hearts?'—revealed exposing those who listened without sincere reflection.
tafsirEn.47:38:
Call to Generosity & the Prophet's ﷺ Praise of Salmān Al-Fārisī (At-Tirmidhī #3261 & Muslim #2546):

📜 When asked who was meant by the people mentioned at the end of this verse, the Prophet ﷺ placed his hand on Salmān Al-Fārisī's shoulder and praised the zeal of his people in attaining faith and knowledge even if it were suspended at the Pleiades.
tafsirEn.13:11:
Guardian Angels & Allāh's Universal Law of Change (Ibn ‘Abbās & Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #555):

📜 Affirms the guardian angels protecting each person by Allāh's command and proclaims the timeless principle: 'Indeed, Allāh will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves.'
tafsirEn.13:12:
Why the Verses of Lightning and Thunder Were Revealed (v.12–13 — At-Tirmidhī #3117 & Al-Muwatta'):

📜 Revealed manifesting Allāh's power in lightning and thunder—which glorifies His praise alongside the angels in awe of Him—and regarding the arrogant envoys ‘Āmir ibn At-Tufayl and Arbad ibn Qays.
tafsirEn.13:17:
The Parable of Truth (Pure Water & Precious Metal) vs. Falsehood (Vanishing Foam):

📜 Likens divine revelation to rain filling valleys according to their capacity: surface foam quickly vanishes like falsehood, while what benefits humanity remains on the earth like enduring Truth.
tafsirEn.13:28:
True Peace of Heart: 'Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allāh hearts are assured!' (v.28–29):

📜 Declares that true serenity and peace of mind are found in remembering Allāh and trusting His promise.
tafsirEn.55:1:
Why Surah Ar-Rahmān Was Revealed & How Ibn Mas‘ūd Recited It Before Quraysh (v.1–13 — At-Tirmidhī #3291):

📜 Revealed when the polytheists asked what 'Ar-Rahmān' meant (25:60), proclaiming that the Most Merciful Himself taught the Quran, created humanity, and endowed them with clear speech. ‘Abdullāh ibn Mas‘ūd was the first companion to recite it aloud by the Ka‘bah. Regarding its refrain repeated thirty-one times ('So which of the favors of your Lord would you both deny?'), the Prophet ﷺ told his companions that when he recited it to the Jinn, each time they heard this verse they responded: 'None of Your favors do we deny, O our Lord; to You belongs all praise!'
tafsirEn.55:19:
The Invisible Barrier Between the Two Seas (Al-Barzakh, v.19–22 — Ibn ‘Abbās):

📜 Highlights Allāh's sign in releasing the two bodies of water (fresh and salt) that meet while maintaining a barrier between them so neither transgresses.
tafsirEn.55:26:
All That Is on Earth Perishes Except Allāh's Countenance & the Four Gardens (v.26–78 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4878 & Muslim #180):

📜 Proclaims Allāh's eternal Majesty and describes the two Gardens of gold and two Gardens of silver prepared for those who feared standing before their Lord.
tafsirEn.65:1:
When and Why Surah At-Talāq Was Revealed & the Verse of Relief (v.1–3 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4908 & Muslim #1471):

📜 Revealed in Madinah establishing the proper regulations and waiting period, illustrated by the Hadith of Ibn ‘Umar. Verses 2–3 proclaim the universal promise: 'And whoever fears Allāh—He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect; and whoever relies upon Allāh—then He is sufficient for him!'
tafsirEn.98:1:
When the Prophet ﷺ Recited Surah Al-Bayyinah to Ubayy ibn Ka‘b (v.1–8 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3809, #4959 & Muslim #799):

📜 Anas ibn Mālik narrated that the Prophet ﷺ told Ubayy ibn Ka‘b: 'Allāh has commanded me to recite Surah Al-Bayyinah to you!' Overcome with joy that Allāh had mentioned him by name, Ubayy wept. The surah affirms that the essence of all divine religion is worshipping Allāh with pure sincerity (v.5), establishing prayer, and paying Zakāt.
tafsirEn.59:1:
When and Why Surah Al-Hashr Was Revealed (Year 4 AH — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4882 & #4884):

📜 Called by Ibn ‘Abbās 'Surah Banū An-Nadīr', it was revealed in Year 4 AH after Banū An-Nadīr broke their covenant by plotting against the Prophet's ﷺ life and fortified themselves in their strongholds; Allāh cast awe into their hearts so that they surrendered and departed into exile without battle.
tafsirEn.59:9:
Context of Verse 9: The Supreme Selflessness (Al-Īthār) of Abū Talhah and Umm Sulaym.

📜 Hadith of Abū Hurayrah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3798, #4889 & Muslim #2054): Revealed regarding Abū Talhah and Umm Sulaym, who put their children to sleep and dimmed the lamp so the Prophet's ﷺ hungry guest could eat their only meal while they spent the night hungry.
tafsirEn.59:22:
The Concluding Verses Exalting Allāh's Most Beautiful Names (v.22–24):

📜 Concludes the surah with over fifteen majestic Names and Attributes of Allāh.
tafsirEn.24:11:
When and Why Verses 11–20 Were Revealed Exonerating ‘Ā'ishah from the Slander (Al-Ifk — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4141, #4750 & Muslim #2770):

📜 Revealed after the expedition of Banū Al-Mustaliq when the hypocrite ‘Abdullāh ibn Ubayy spread a false slander against the Mother of the Believers ‘Ā'ishah; Allāh sent down these ten verses from above the seven heavens declaring her complete innocence and purity.
tafsirEn.24:22:
When and Why Verse 22 Was Revealed: Abū Bakr's Forgiveness of Mistah ('Would You Not Love That Allāh Should Forgive You?').

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #2661, #4750 & Muslim #2770): After Allāh revealed verses 11–21 clearing **‘Ā'ishah** of the slander (*Al-Ifk*), **Abū Bakr As-Siddīq** vowed to stop supporting his poor relative Mistah who had repeated the rumor. When Allāh revealed: 'Let them pardon and overlook! Would you not love that Allāh should forgive you?', Abū Bakr wept and said: 'Yes indeed, by Allāh, I love that Allāh should forgive me!' and restored Mistah's allowance forever.
tafsirEn.24:35:
The Verse of Light (Āyat an-Nūr, v.35–38 — Exegesis of Ubayy ibn Ka‘b & Ibn ‘Abbās):

📜 Allāh is the Light of the heavens and the earth, and the parable of His light in the heart of the sincere believer is like a niche containing a radiant lamp within crystal fueled by a blessed olive tree—'Light upon Light'.
tafsirEn.22:1:
Context of Surah Al-Hajj & the Convulsion of the Hour (v.1–2 — At-Tirmidhī #3168 & Ahmad):

📜 Combining both Makkan and Madinan revelations, its opening verses warning of the mighty earthquake of the Hour descended while the Prophet ﷺ was traveling with his companions, moving them to tears as he explained the Day of Resurrection.
tafsirEn.22:19:
When and Why Verses 19–22 Were Revealed Regarding the Six Duelists at the Opening of Badr.

📜 Hadith of Abū Dharr & ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4743, #4744 & Muslim #3033): Revealed regarding **Hamzah**, **‘Alī**, and **‘Ubaydah ibn Al-Hārith** who went forth to face the three champions of Quraysh at the start of the Battle of Badr.
tafsirEn.22:39:
The First Verse Revealed Permitting Self-Defense for the Oppressed (v.39–40 — At-Tirmidhī #3171 & An-Nasā'ī #3085):

📜 Ibn ‘Abbās explained that after more than thirteen years of patient endurance under persecution in Makkah, this was the very first verse revealed permitting the believers to defend themselves after being unjustly driven from their homes solely for saying 'Our Lord is Allāh,' protecting monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques where Allāh's Name is remembered.
tafsirEn.63:1:
When and Why Surah Al-Munāfiqūn Was Revealed Confirming Zayd ibn Arqam's Truthfulness (v.1–8 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4900, #4901 & Muslim #2772):

📜 Revealed during the expedition of Banū Al-Mustaliq when the hypocrite chief ‘Abdullāh ibn Ubayy said: 'Do not spend on those with Allāh's Messenger until they disband, and if we return to Madinah the more honorable will expel the meaner!' When young Zayd ibn Arqam reported this and Ibn Ubayy swore falsely to deny it, Allāh revealed this surah quoting his exact words; the Prophet ﷺ gently held Zayd's ear and said: 'O boy, your ear was true and Allāh has confirmed your words!'
tafsirEn.58:1:
Context of Verses 1–4: The Plea of Khawlah bint Tha‘labah Heard from Above the Seven Heavens.

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī, Ibn Mājah #2063 & Musnad Ahmad): Revealed when Khawlah bint Tha‘labah pleaded with the Prophet ﷺ after her husband Aws ibn As-Sāmit pronounced the pre-Islamic formula of Zihār; Allāh heard her plea from above the seven heavens and ordained the expiation to preserve their family.
tafsirEn.58:11:
Context of Verse 11: Making Room in Gatherings for the Veterans of Badr and Elevating People of Knowledge.

📜 Account of Muqātil & Qatādah (At-Tabarī & Ibn Kathīr): Revealed on a Friday when veterans of Badr arrived at a crowded gathering around the Prophet ﷺ, commanding believers to make room generously and declaring that Allāh raises in degrees those who believe and those given knowledge.
tafsirEn.49:1:
When and Why Verses 1–5 Were Revealed on Reverence for the Prophet ﷺ (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4845, #4847 & Muslim #119):

📜 Revealed teaching etiquette in the presence of the Messenger ﷺ and when the delegation of Banū Tamīm called out loudly from behind his private chambers; the Prophet ﷺ reassured Thābit ibn Qays (whose natural voice was loud) that he belongs to the people of Paradise.
tafsirEn.49:6:
Context of Verses 6–8: The Golden Rule of Verifying News Before Acting (At-Tabayyun).

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās, Qatādah & Al-Hārith ibn Dirār (Musnad Ahmad & At-Tabarī): Revealed when Al-Walīd ibn ‘Uqbah mistakenly thought the tribe of Banū Al-Mustaliq was coming out to fight him when they were actually coming out to welcome him; Allāh commanded verifying all reports carefully so that no people are harmed out of ignorance.
tafsirEn.49:11:
Brotherhood, Forbidding Mockery and Backbiting, & Universal Human Equality (v.11–13 — At-Tirmidhī #3270):

📜 Prohibits mockery, offensive nicknames, suspicion, and backbiting, and culminates in verse 13: 'O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allāh is the most righteous of you!'
tafsirEn.66:1:
Context of Verses 1–5: The Vow to Abstain from Honey and the Admonition to the Prophet's ﷺ Wives.

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah & Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4912, #4913 & Muslim #1474): Revealed when the Prophet ﷺ vowed to stop drinking honey to please his wives, gently reminding him not to forbid what Allāh made lawful and ordaining the expiation for oaths.
tafsirEn.66:10:
The Parables of Accountability & the Perfection of Āsiyah and Maryam (v.10–12 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3411 & Muslim #2431):

📜 Shows that faith is personal: the wives of Nūh and Lūt were not availed by their marriage to Prophets because of their betrayal of faith, whereas Āsiyah (wife of Pharaoh) and Maryam bint ‘Imrān attained the highest pinnacle of faith and honor.
tafsirEn.64:1:
Why Surah At-Taghābun Was Revealed in Madinah (v.1–10 — At-Tirmidhī #3316):

📜 Reminds humanity of Allāh's perfect creation, warns against worldly distractions of wealth and children, and describes Judgment Day as Yawm at-Taghābun (the Day of Mutual Disillusionment/Cheating) where the wrongdoers regret deeply.
tafsirEn.61:1:
Why Surah As-Saff Was Revealed: The Love for Unified Rows (v.1–4 — At-Tirmidhī #3309):

📜 Revealed when companions asked which deed is most beloved to Allāh; Allāh revealed: 'Indeed, Allāh loves those who fight in His cause in a row as if they are a solid cemented structure.'
tafsirEn.62:1:
Prescription of Friday Prayer & Blaming Distraction (v.9–11 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #2064 & Muslim #863):

📜 Revealed when a trade caravan arrived in Madinah on a Friday while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the sermon, causing many attendees to rush out except for twelve loyal men; Allāh taught that what He has with Him of reward and provision is far better than idle entertainment.
tafsirEn.48:1:
Context of Verses 1–5: The Revelation of Surah Al-Fath Returning from Al-Hudaybiyah.

📜 Hadith of ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattāb & Al-Barā' (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4172, #4833 & Muslim #1786): Revealed on the return journey from the Treaty of Al-Hudaybiyah, naming the peace treaty a 'Clear Victory' (*Fathan Mubīnā*) that opened the path to the peaceful spread of Islam and the Conquest of Makkah.
tafsirEn.5:3:
When and Where the Verse of Completion of Religion Was Revealed (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #45 & Muslim #3017):

📜 Revealed in Madinah during the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat al-Wadā‘) on Friday afternoon at ‘Arafāt in Year 10 AH. When a Jewish man told ‘Umar that if this verse ('Today I have perfected for you your religion...') had been revealed to the Jews they would have taken that day as a festival, ‘Umar confirmed the exact day and time of its descent.
tafsirEn.9:1:
When and Why Surah At-Tawbah Was Revealed in Year 9 AH Without Basmalah (v.1–5 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4363, #4655 & At-Tirmidhī #3086):

📜 Revealed in Year 9 AH after the expedition of Tabūk; the Prophet ﷺ sent Abū Bakr to lead the Hajj and dispatched ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib to proclaim its opening verses at Minā terminating treaties with treacherous polytheist tribes while honoring until their full term the treaties of those who remained faithful (v.4).
tafsirEn.9:40:
The Cave of Thawr During the Hijrah: 'Do Not Grieve; Indeed, Allāh Is With Us!'

📜 Hadith of Abū Bakr As-Siddīq & Anas (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3653 & Muslim #2381): Immortalizes the moment in the Cave of Thawr when the trackers of Quraysh stood right above them and the Prophet ﷺ reassured Abū Bakr: *'What do you think of two when Allāh is their Third?'*
tafsirEn.9:60:
The Eight Exclusive Categories of Zakāt Recipients (Abū Dāwūd #1630):

📜 Defines the eight rightful categories for obligatory charity: the poor, the needy, collectors, those whose hearts are reconciled, freeing captives, overburdened debtors, in Allāh's cause, and the stranded traveler.
tafsirEn.9:117:
When and How Allāh's Repentance Was Revealed for Ka‘b ibn Mālik and His Two Companions (v.117–119 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4418 & Muslim #2769):

📜 After praising the Prophet ﷺ, the Muhājirūn, and the Ansār who endured the hardship of Tabūk (v.117), Allāh revealed verse 118 pardoning the three truthful companions (Ka‘b ibn Mālik, Murārah ibn Ar-Rabī‘, and Hilāl ibn Umayyah) who had stayed behind without excuse yet spoke the complete truth, concluding: 'O you who have believed, fear Allāh and be with those who are true!' (v.119).
tafsirEn.110:1:
When and Why Surah An-Nasr Was Revealed: The Final Complete Surah & Sign of the Prophet's ﷺ Passing (v.1–3 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4970, #4967 & Muslim #3024, #484):

📜 Ibn ‘Abbās and Ibn ‘Umar confirmed that this is the very last complete surah revealed. When ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattāb asked the veterans of Badr and young Ibn ‘Abbās about its meaning, Ibn ‘Abbās explained that it was Allāh's notification to His Messenger ﷺ that the completion of his mission—marked by the Conquest of Makkah and people entering Islam in multitudes—signaled the approach of his passing, commanding him to glorify his Lord's praise and seek forgiveness. ‘Ā'ishah narrated that thereafter the Prophet ﷺ constantly recited in his bowing and prostration: 'Subhānaka Allāhumma Rabbanā wa bi-hamdika, Allāhumma ighfir lī!'
tafsirEn.92:1:
When and Why Surah Al-Layl Was Revealed Regarding Abū Bakr As-Siddīq (v.1–21 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4949 & Muslim #2647):

📜 Contrasts the generous believer eased toward goodness with the miserly, and concludes with verses 17–21 revealed in honor of Abū Bakr As-Siddīq, who spent his wealth in Makkah to purchase and free persecuted believers such as Bilāl solely seeking the Face of his Lord the Most High.
tafsirEn.89:1:
The Ten Blessed Nights of Dhū al-Hijjah & the Tranquil Soul (v.1–30 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #969):

📜 Swears by the Dawn and the Ten Nights of Dhū al-Hijjah, recounts the fate of ‘Ād, Thamūd, and Pharaoh, and concludes with the call to the reassured soul (An-Nafs al-Mutma'innah, v.27–30) to enter among Allāh's righteous servants and His Paradise.
tafsirEn.93:1:
When and Why Surah Ad-Duhā Was Revealed to Console the Prophet ﷺ (v.1–11 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4950 & Muslim #1797):

📜 Jundub ibn Sufyān narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ was unwell for two nights and polytheists claimed his Lord had forsaken him, Allāh revealed Surah Ad-Duhā swearing by the morning brightness: 'Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested you! And the Hereafter is better for you than the first life, and your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied!'
tafsirEn.94:1:
Why Surah Ash-Sharh Was Revealed in Makkah (v.1–8 — Sahīh Muslim #162):

📜 Reminds the Prophet ﷺ of Allāh expanding his breast with light, removing his heavy burden, and exalting his mention alongside Allāh's Name, proclaiming twice that with every hardship comes ease (v.5–6).
tafsirEn.103:1:
Surah Al-‘Asr: The Four Pillars of Human Salvation (v.1–3 — Imam Ash-Shāfi‘ī):

📜 Summarizes the entire path to salvation in faith, righteous deeds, mutual encouragement to Truth, and mutual encouragement to patience; the companions used to recite it to one another whenever they parted.
tafsirEn.100:1:
Why Surah Al-‘Ādiyāt Was Revealed (v.1–11 — Ibn ‘Abbās):

📜 Swears by the charging steeds striking sparks at dawn that man is ungrateful to his Lord and overly attached to worldly wealth, forgetting the Day when the graves are overturned and the secrets of hearts are laid bare.
tafsirEn.82:1:
Le fendillement du ciel et les nobles Anges scribes (Kirāmin Kātibīn, v.1-19) :

Rappelle à l'homme la générosité de son Créateur qui l'a façonné harmonieusement, la surveillance des Anges scribes qui consignent tout, et le Jour où nul ne détiendra aucun pouvoir pour autrui.
tafsirEn.84:1:
Le déchirement du ciel et la remise des feuillets (v.1-25) :

📜 Hadith de ‘Ā'ishah (Al-Bukhārī n°103 & Muslim n°2876) : Au sujet du verset 8 (« Il subira un jugement facile »), le Prophète ﷺ expliqua qu'il s'agit de la simple présentation des œuvres avec le pardon d'Allāh, car quiconque se voit discuter en détail ses comptes est châtié.
tafsirEn.88:1:
L'Enveloppante (Al-Ghāshiyah, v.1-26) :

Oppose l'humiliation des damnés aux visages radieux des élus au Paradis, et appelle à méditer le miracle de la création du chameau, du ciel, des montagnes et de la terre (v.17-20).
tafsirEn.7:31:
When and Why Verses 31–32 Were Revealed Abolishing Pre-Islamic Practices Around the Ka‘bah.

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Muslim #3028): In pre-Islamic times, certain tribes performed *Tawāf* around the Ka‘bah naked while forbidding themselves pure foods; Allāh revealed: *'O Children of Adam, take your adornment (decent clothing) at every mosque!'*
tafsirEn.7:46:
Les Gens d'Al-A‘rāf (les hauteurs entre le Paradis et l'Enfer, v.46-49) :

📜 D'après Ibn Mas‘ūd, Hudhayfah et Ibn ‘Abbās, les gens d'Al-A‘rāf sont des croyants dont les bonnes et les mauvaises actions se sont trouvées strictement égales dans la Balance : retenus temporairement sur la muraille surplombant le Paradis et l'Enfer, ils implorent la miséricorde de leur Seigneur jusqu'à ce qu'Allāh les fasse entrer au Paradis par Sa grâce.
tafsirEn.7:54: La Majesté du Créateur établi sur le Trône et l'invocation dans l'humilité (v.54-56).
tafsirEn.7:59: La grande fresque historique des Prophètes : Nūh (v.59-64), Hūd chez les ‘Ād (v.65-72), Sālih chez les Thamūd (v.73-79), Lūt (v.80-84), Shu‘ayb à Madyan (v.85-93) et Mūsā face à Pharaon et aux magiciens (v.103-171).
tafsirEn.7:157:
L'annonce du Prophète illettré Muhammad ﷺ dans la Torah et l'Évangile :

Celui qui leur ordonne le convenable, leur interdit le blâmable, leur rend licites les bonnes choses, leur interdit les mauvaises et leur ôte le joug et les chaînes qui pesaient sur eux.
tafsirEn.7:204:
L'écoute recueillie du Coran (v.204) et le verset de prosternation finale (v.206) :

« Et quand on récite le Coran, prêtez-lui l'oreille attentivement et observez le silence, afin que vous obteniez miséricorde ! »
tafsirEn.79:1:
Context of Surah An-Nāzi‘āt in Makkah (v.1–14):

📜 Revealed to affirm the reality of the Resurrection, Allāh swears by the angels who violently snatch the souls of the disbelievers and those who gently draw out the souls of the believers, confirming that the first and second blasts of the Trumpet will surely occur.
tafsirEn.79:42:
Why the Final Verses About the Hour Were Revealed (v.42–46 — Sahīh Al-Bukhārī & Muslim):

📜 Revealed when the polytheists constantly questioned the Prophet ﷺ about the exact time of the Hour out of mockery. Allāh declared that knowledge of its exact time belongs exclusively to Him, and that the Prophet's ﷺ role is solely to warn those who fear it.
tafsirEn.2:125:
‘Umar ibn Al-Khattāb's Agreement with Revelation Regarding Maqām Ibrāhīm.

📜 Hadith of ‘Umar (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #402 & Muslim #2399): ‘Umar stated that his view coincided with his Lord's decree in three matters, including his suggestion to take the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer just before verse 125 was revealed.
tafsirEn.2:207:
Suhayb Ar-Rūmī Giving Up All His Wealth for Allāh's Pleasure During the Hijrah.

📜 Account of Sa‘īd ibn Al-Musayyib & Anas (Al-Hākim): Pursued by Quraysh while emigrating to Madinah, Suhayb surrendered all his hidden gold in Makkah to safeguard his faith; upon his arrival, the Prophet ﷺ congratulated him on this blessed trade mentioned in verse 207.
tafsirEn.5:6:
The Institution of Dry Ablution (At-Tayammum) as Divine Ease.

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #334 & Muslim #367): When the army camped without water while searching for ‘Ā'ishah's lost necklace and dawn prayer arrived, Allāh revealed the concession of Tayammum with clean earth as a mercy for the entire Ummah.
tafsirEn.5:67:
Allāh's Guaranteed Protection of His Messenger ﷺ.

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah (At-Tirmidhī #3046): Companions used to guard the Prophet's ﷺ tent at night until this verse descended guaranteeing Allāh's protection from people, whereupon the Prophet ﷺ thanked and dismissed his guards.
tafsirEn.5:90:
The Final Prohibition of Intoxicants and Gambling (v.90–91).

📜 Hadith of ‘Umar & Anas (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4617 & Muslim #1980): Following ‘Umar's supplication for a decisive ruling on wine, Allāh revealed verses 90–91 asking 'Will you then abstain?', to which ‘Umar proclaimed: 'We have abstained, O Lord!'
tafsirEn.9:84:
Prohibition of Praying Over Those Who Die in Confirmed Hypocrisy.

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Umar (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #1269 & Muslim #2400): Revealed after the death of ‘Abdullāh ibn Ubayy, permanently forbidding funeral prayer over confirmed hypocrites.
tafsirEn.9:102:
Acceptance of the Repentance of Abū Lubābah (v.102–103).

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās (At-Tabarī): Revealed pardoning Abū Lubābah and those who acknowledged their sins after tying themselves to a pillar of the Mosque in remorse.
tafsirEn.24:31:
Immediate Obedience of the Believing Women Upon the Revelation of Modesty.

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4758): ‘Ā'ishah praised the women of the Muhājirūn and Ansār who immediately covered themselves with thick garments at dawn as soon as this verse was revealed.
tafsirEn.24:61:
Removing Hardship in Sharing Meals with the Blind, the Lame, the Sick, and Relatives.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās (Abū Dāwūd #3772): Revealed to lift excessive scruples that prevented people from dining with the disabled or in the homes of close relatives.
tafsirEn.2:3:
The Attributes of the Pious (Al-Muttaqūn): Belief in the Unseen, Prayer, and Charity.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn Mas‘ūd & Ibn ‘Abbās: Those who believe in the Unseen (Al-Ghayb—Allāh, His Angels, Paradise, Hell, and the Resurrection), establish regular prayer with humility, and spend in charity from what Allāh has provided them.
tafsirEn.2:4:
Completing Faith: Belief in All Revealed Scriptures and Certainty in the Hereafter (v.4–5).

📜 Hadith of Abū Mūsā Al-Ash‘arī (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #97 & Muslim #154): Praises those who believe in what was revealed to Muhammad ﷺ and what was revealed to the Prophets before him, affirming that those among the People of the Book who believe in their Prophet and then believe in Muhammad ﷺ receive a double reward.
tafsirEn.2:6:
Why Verses 6–7 Were Revealed Regarding the Stubborn Chiefs of Disbelief.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Ar-Rabī‘ ibn Anas: Revealed regarding the obstinate leaders of disbelief (such as Abū Jahl and the chiefs who persisted in denial despite recognizing the truth), whose hearts and hearing were sealed because of their persistent arrogance.
tafsirEn.68:2:
Divine Exoneration of the Prophet ﷺ from Every False Accusation.

📜 By the grace of your Lord—through Prophethood and Wisdom—you are completely free of what the disbelievers of Quraysh falsely claim.
tafsirEn.68:3:
An Unceasing, Eternal Reward for the Prophet's ﷺ Patience.

📜 Allāh assures His Messenger ﷺ that his steadfastness in conveying the Message brings an immense reward that will never be cut off or diminished (Ghayra mamnūn).
tafsirEn.68:5:
Truth vs. Falsehood Will Soon Be Seen by All (v.5–6).

📜 Proclaims that both the believers and the mockers of Quraysh will soon behold on the Day of Badr and on Judgment Day who was truly astray.
tafsirEn.68:6:
Which of You Is Truly Afflicted with Madness and Delusion.

📜 Exposes the delusion of the idolaters who rejected pure Monotheism while accusing the noblest of creation ﷺ.
tafsirEn.68:7:
Allāh Alone Knows Best Those Who Stray and Those Who Are Guided.

📜 Consoles the Prophet ﷺ by reminding him that Allāh fully knows the inner state of every heart.
tafsirEn.68:8:
Command to Stand Firm and Never Yield to the Deniers.

📜 Forbids any compromise in religion with the chiefs of Quraysh who rejected the Message.
tafsirEn.68:9:
Why Verse 9 Was Revealed: Rejecting Compromises in Monotheism.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: The polytheists of Makkah wished that the Prophet ﷺ would soften his stance toward their idols so they might soften toward him; Allāh forbade any concession at the expense of pure Tawhīd.
tafsirEn.68:10:
Warning Against Obeying Every Habitual, Worthless Swearer (v.10–16).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah: Revealed describing the arrogant enemies of Truth in Makkah (such as Al-Walīd ibn Al-Mughīrah or Al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq) who swore false oaths abundantly.
tafsirEn.68:11:
Condemnation of Slander and Spreading Malicious Gossip (Namīmah).

📜 Hadith of Hudhayfah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #6056 & Muslim #105): Warns against the backbiter (Hammāz) who walks about spreading malicious tales (Mashshā'in bi-namīm) to divide people.
tafsirEn.68:12:
The Hinderer of Every Good, Transgressor, and Sinner.

📜 Describes the enemy of Islam who aggressively prevented his family and followers from accepting faith and spending in charity.
tafsirEn.68:14:
Arrogance Triggered by Worldly Wealth and Sons (v.13–14).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Instead of thanking Allāh for granting him abundant wealth and ten sons, Al-Walīd ibn Al-Mughīrah used those blessings to rebel against Allāh's Messenger ﷺ.
tafsirEn.68:15:
Dismissing the Divine Revelations as 'Tales of the Ancients'.

📜 When the verses of the Quran were recited to him, he arrogantly claimed they were merely legends of former peoples.
tafsirEn.68:19:
The Nighttime Visitation That Consumed the Garden While They Slept (v.19–20).

📜 Because of their unjust intention to deprive the poor, Allāh sent a visitation from the sky by night while they were asleep.
tafsirEn.68:21:
Calling Out to One Another at Daybreak (v.21–22).

📜 Unaware of what had befallen their orchard, they called one another early in the morning to hurry to their harvest.
tafsirEn.68:22:
Setting Out Early to Reap the Fruits Before the Poor Could Arrive.

📜 They urged one another to go forth at dawn if they intended to gather the crop in secret.
tafsirEn.68:23:
Whispering in Secret to Exclude the Needy (v.23–24).

📜 They walked whispering to one another so that no poor person would hear their footsteps.
tafsirEn.68:24:
Their Unjust Resolution: 'Let Not a Single Needy Person Enter Upon You Today!'

📜 Exposes the hardness of heart when greed blinds people to the rights of the poor.
tafsirEn.68:25:
Going Forth Confident in Their Ability to Deprive the Poor.

📜 They went out early assuming they held complete power over their wealth, forgetting the Decree of Allāh.
tafsirEn.68:26:
Shock Upon Seeing the Ruined Garden: 'Indeed, We Have Lost Our Way!' (v.26–27).

📜 When they saw the blackened land, they first thought they had taken the wrong path before realizing the truth.
tafsirEn.68:27:
Realizing Their Loss: 'Rather, We Have Been Deprived!'

📜 Having intended to deprive the poor, they themselves were deprived of the entire harvest.
tafsirEn.68:28:
The Most Upright Brother's Reminder: 'Did I Not Tell You to Glorify Allāh?'

📜 The wisest among them reminded his brothers that he had warned them to glorify Allāh, say In shā'a Allāh, and fear Him.
tafsirEn.68:29:
Their Repentance and Confession: 'Exalted Is Our Lord! Indeed, We Were Wrongdoers!'

📜 Awakening from their heedlessness, they glorified Allāh and confessed their injustice.
tafsirEn.68:30:
Mutual Admonition and Sincere Regret (v.30–32).

📜 They turned to one another acknowledging their transgression in plotting against the rights of the needy.
tafsirEn.68:31:
Confessing Their Transgression: 'Woe to Us! Indeed, We Were Transgressors!'

📜 Acknowledging that withholding the right of the poor was an act of rebellion against Allāh's blessing.
tafsirEn.68:32:
Hoping in Allāh's Mercy: 'Perhaps Our Lord Will Substitute for Us a Better Garden!'

📜 Turning back to their Lord in hope and repentance, seeking His pardon and a better compensation.
tafsirEn.68:33:
The Lesson of Worldly Trials Compared to the Hereafter.

📜 Such is the warning punishment in this world so people may repent, while the punishment of the Hereafter is far greater if they only knew.
tafsirEn.68:34:
The Promise of the Gardens of Delight for the God-Fearing (v.34–35).

📜 Contrasts the fleeting worldly orchard with the eternal Gardens of Bliss prepared for those who fear Allāh.
tafsirEn.68:35:
Divine Justice: 'Shall We Then Treat the Muslims Like the Criminals?' (v.35–36).

📜 Refutes the false claim of the Makkan polytheists who asserted that even if there were a Resurrection, they would be given better than the believers.
tafsirEn.68:36:
Rebuking Corrupt Judgment: 'What Is the Matter with You? How Do You Judge?'

📜 Condemns the crooked logic of equating the obedient believer with the defiant idolater.
tafsirEn.68:37:
Challenging Their Baseless Claims (v.37–38).

📜 Asks whether they possess any revealed Scripture guaranteeing them whatever they desire.
tafsirEn.68:38:
Exposing Their Wishful Illusions About the Hereafter.

📜 Shows that their claims are built on mere conjecture rather than any divine promise.
tafsirEn.68:39:
Or Have You Binding Covenants with Allāh Until Judgment Day? (v.39–41).

📜 Silences the polytheists by asking if they hold any covenant from Allāh or any partners who can guarantee their claims.
tafsirEn.68:40:
'Ask Them Which of Them Will Guarantee That!'

📜 Challenges their leaders who claimed they would bear the sins of their followers on Judgment Day.
tafsirEn.68:41:
Let Them Bring Forth Their False Partners If They Are Truthful!

📜 Establishes the utter helplessness of false deities on the Day of Account.
tafsirEn.68:44:
'So Leave Me with Whoever Denies This Quran!' (v.44–45).

📜 A severe warning to those who persist in denying the Quran while mistaking Allāh's respite for immunity (Istidrāj).
tafsirEn.68:45:
Divine Respite (Al-Imlā') and the Infallible Plan of Allāh.

📜 Allāh grants them time so they may either repent or face His unassailable decree.
tafsirEn.68:46:
The Prophet ﷺ Asks No Worldly Wage (v.46–47).

📜 Affirms that the Messenger ﷺ seeks no payment from them, nor do they possess knowledge of the Unseen.
tafsirEn.68:47:
No Access to the Unseen.

📜 None of the deniers possess the Tablet of the Unseen from which they could write down their own destiny.
tafsirEn.68:49:
Command to Be Patient & the Example of Yūnus (Jonah, v.48–50).

📜 Commands the Prophet ﷺ to endure patiently his Lord's decree and not be hasty like the Companion of the Whale (Yūnus, peace be upon him), whom Allāh reached with His grace and chose among the righteous after his heartfelt supplication in the darkness.
tafsirEn.68:50:
Allāh's Choice of Yūnus Among the Righteous.

📜 Highlights how Allāh accepted Yūnus's repentance and elevated him among His righteous Messengers.
tafsirEn.68:52:
Why Verses 51–52 Were Revealed: Protection from the Evil Eye & theUniversal Reminder.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās, Mujāhid & Qatādah: When the disbelievers of Quraysh heard the Quran, they glared at the Prophet ﷺ with intense hatred and envy, nearly making him slip with their eyes, while calling him mad; Allāh protected him and declared: 'And it is nothing less than a Reminder for all the worlds!'
tafsirEn.73:3:
The Choice of Half the Night, a Third, or Two-Thirds.

📜 Grants flexibility between half the night, one-third, or two-thirds in night devotion.
tafsirEn.73:5:
Why Night Prayer Was Ordained: Preparing for the 'Weighty Word' (Al-Qawl ath-Thaqīl).

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #2): Allāh prepared the Prophet's ﷺ heart through night prayer to receive the weighty revelation of the Quran and its obligations; ‘Ā'ishah recounted that even on a bitterly cold day, when revelation descended upon him, his forehead would glisten with sweat.
tafsirEn.73:6:
Why the Hours of the Night Are Most Effective for the Heart and Speech.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Anas: Rising in the quiet of the night brings the heart and the tongue into harmony, free from the noise and distractions of the day.
tafsirEn.73:7:
Daytime Striving and Responsibilities.

📜 During the day, the believer is occupied with conveying the Message and earning a livelihood, making the night the prime sanctuary for prolonged devotion.
tafsirEn.73:8:
Remembering the Name of Your Lord and Devoting Yourself Wholly to Him (At-Tabattul).

📜 Calls for sincere devotion to Allāh alone in worship and supplication while fulfilling one's duties in the world.
tafsirEn.73:9:
Lord of the East and the West: Taking Him Alone as Disposer of Affairs (Al-Wakīl).

📜 Since there is no deity except Allāh, Sovereign of all horizons, the believer entrusts all matters solely to Him.
tafsirEn.73:10:
Patient Endurance and Gracious Avoidance of the Mockers (Al-Hajr al-Jamīl).

📜 Commands the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah to bear patiently what the polytheists say and to part from them in a dignified, gracious manner without retaliation.
tafsirEn.73:11:
'And Leave Me with the Deniers, Possessors of Luxury!'

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Revealed regarding the wealthy chiefs of Quraysh (such as the leaders of Banū Al-Mughīrah) who mocked the Prophet ﷺ; Allāh sufficed him against them at Badr.
tafsirEn.73:12:
The Warning of Shackles and the Blazing Fire in the Hereafter (v.12–13).

📜 Warns the arrogant deniers of the heavy fetters and choking punishment awaiting them on Judgment Day.
tafsirEn.73:13:
Choking Food and a Painful Torment.

📜 Contrasts the fleeting luxuries they enjoyed in disobedience with the bitter recompense of the Hereafter.
tafsirEn.73:14:
The Day the Earth and the Mountains Quake.

📜 Describes the Day of Resurrection when the solid mountains are turned into heaps of shifting, pouring sand.
tafsirEn.73:15:
The Parallel Between the Mission of Muhammad ﷺ and Mūsā (v.15–16).

📜 Reminds Quraysh that just as Allāh sent a Messenger (Mūsā) to Pharaoh—who rebelled and was seized with a severe punishment—He has sent Muhammad ﷺ as a witness and warner to them.
tafsirEn.73:16:
Pharaoh's Disobedience to the Messenger and His Ruin.

📜 Serves as a historical warning to the chiefs of Makkah lest they follow Pharaoh's path of arrogance.
tafsirEn.73:17:
The Day That Turns Children Gray-Haired (v.17–18).

📜 Depicts the overwhelming awe of the Day of Resurrection when the sky is cleft asunder and Allāh's promise is fulfilled.
tafsirEn.73:18:
The Splitting of the Sky & the Fulfillment of Allāh's Promise.

📜 Even the vast heavens cleave apart out of reverence for the Majesty of Allāh on that Day.
tafsirEn.73:19:
An Open Reminder for Whoever Wills to Take a Path to His Lord.

📜 Declares that these verses are a reminder so that every sincere soul may choose the path of faith and obedience leading to Allāh.
tafsirEn.74:2:
The Divine Command to Arise and Warn Humanity (v.2–3).

📜 Hadith of Jābir ibn ‘Abdillāh (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4922 & Muslim #161): After the initial revelation in the Cave of Hirā', when Angel Jibrīl appeared sitting on a throne between the sky and the earth, the Prophet ﷺ returned home trembling and asked Khadījah to wrap him up; Allāh then revealed these verses commanding him to transition from personal preparation to public proclamation and warning.
tafsirEn.74:3:
And Your Lord Alone Glorify (Takbīr).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah: Commands the Prophet ﷺ to proclaim that his Lord is far greater than any false deity or idol worshipped by Quraysh, establishing the foundation of *Allāhu Akbar* in prayer and call.
tafsirEn.74:4:
Purification of Garments, Heart, and Conduct.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās, Mujāhid & Ash-Shāfi‘ī: Combines both physical purity—keeping one's garments clean from filth for prayer—and spiritual purity, keeping one's character, actions, and soul free from sin and treachery.
tafsirEn.74:5:
Forsaking All Forms of Idolatry and Sin (Ar-Rujz).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: *Ar-Rujz* refers to the idols of pre-Islamic Makkah (such as Isāf and Nā'ilah) and every form of polytheism and disobedience; persevering in abandoning them draws the believer closer to Allāh.
tafsirEn.74:6:
Giving Purely for Allāh Without Seeking Worldly Return.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Al-Hasan Al-Basrī: Instructs the Messenger ﷺ never to give a gift in order to receive more in return, nor to consider his own deeds and sacrifices as a favor upon his Lord, but rather to act solely out of gratitude to Allāh.
tafsirEn.74:7:
Steadfast Patience for the Sake of Your Lord.

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid & Ibn Zayd: Commands the Prophet ﷺ to endure the hostility and persecution of his people purely seeking the Face of his Lord.
tafsirEn.74:8:
The Sounding of the Trumpet (An-Nāqūr, v.8–10).

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās & Abū Sa‘īd Al-Khudrī (At-Tirmidhī #2431): *An-Nāqūr* is the Horn into which Angel Isrāfīl will blow to herald the Resurrection; the Prophet ﷺ said: 'How can I enjoy ease when the Angel of the Horn has placed the Horn to his lips and inclined his forehead, waiting for the command to blow?'
tafsirEn.74:9:
The Terror of That Difficult Day.

📜 Describes the Day of Judgment as a Day of intense distress and hardship for those who turned away from Allāh's guidance.
tafsirEn.74:10:
Devoid of Any Ease for the Disbelievers.

📜 While Allāh lightens the standing of Judgment Day for the sincere believers (making it as brief as an obligatory prayer), it remains heavy and relentless for those who died in disbelief.
tafsirEn.74:11:
When and Why Verses 11–26 Were Revealed Regarding Al-Walīd ibn Al-Mughīrah.

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās & ‘Ikrimah (Al-Hākim, Al-Bayhaqī & At-Tabarī): Allāh says: 'Leave Me alone with him whom I created alone'—referring to **Al-Walīd ibn Al-Mughīrah** (dubbed 'the Unique' among Quraysh for his wealth and status), who emerged from his mother's womb without wealth or children and will return to Allāh's judgment alone.
tafsirEn.74:12:
Vast Wealth Bestowed in Makkah and At-Tā'if.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: Allāh granted Al-Walīd vast herds, trade caravans, and orchards stretching between Makkah and At-Tā'if that yielded continuous harvests year-round.
tafsirEn.74:13:
Sons Always Present by His Side (Shuhūdā).

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid & Qatādah: He was given ten or more sons in Makkah who never had to travel for trade because his immense wealth sufficed them at home—three of whom later embraced Islam (**Khālid ibn Al-Walīd**, Al-Walīd, and Hishām).
tafsirEn.74:14:
Every Worldly Comfort and Authority Made Smooth for Him.

📜 Allāh granted him longevity, prestige, and leadership among his tribe, yet he met these favors with ingratitude.
tafsirEn.74:15:
His Vain Greed for Even More Without Faith.

📜 Despite his rejection of the Quran, he arrogantly claimed that if Paradise existed he would be given even more wealth and children there.
tafsirEn.74:16:
His Stubborn Defiance Against Allāh's Clear Signs (v.16–17).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Because he knowingly opposed the verses of the Quran after recognizing their truth, Allāh decreed that his wealth and sons would steadily decline until he faced the steep, exhausting ascent of punishment in the Hereafter (Sa‘ūdā).
tafsirEn.74:18:
