How Al-Walīd Plotted Against the Quran After Admitting Its Sweetness (v.18–25).

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās (Al-Hākim #3872 & At-Tabarī): After listening to the Prophet ﷺ recite Surah Fussilat, Al-Walīd told Quraysh: 'By Allāh, I have heard from Muhammad words that are neither the speech of men nor of jinn! Indeed, it has a sweetness, and upon it is a splendor; its highest part is fruitful and its lowest part is gushing with abundance, and it triumphs and is never surpassed!' Yet when Abū Jahl pressured him to denounce it before the pilgrims arrived, Al-Walīd sat pondering and plotting how to label it.
tafsirEn.74:19:
Condemnation of His Deliberate Scheming Against the Truth.

📜 Rebukes him for knowingly fabricating a false accusation against Allāh's Word merely to please his tribe and preserve his status.
tafsirEn.74:20:
Repeated Woe Upon One Who Rejects Truth After Seeing It.

📜 Emphasizes the gravity of turning away from divine guidance out of pride after one's own conscience has testified to its truth.
tafsirEn.74:21:
Surveying the Claims of Soothsaying, Madness, and Poetry.

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās: When Quraysh suggested calling Muhammad ﷺ a kahin (soothsayer), a madman, or a poet, Al-Walīd rejected all three because he knew every meter of Arabic poetry and saw that the Quran transcended them all.
tafsirEn.74:22:
Frowning and Scowling in Frustration.

📜 Unable to find any genuine flaw in the Quran, his face darkened and contorted as he chose falsehood over truth.
tafsirEn.74:23:
Turning His Back on Faith Out of Arrogance.

📜 He turned away from embracing Islam out of haughtiness and fear of losing his standing among Quraysh.
tafsirEn.74:24:
His False Verdict: 'This Is Nothing But Magic Handed Down!'

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās: To deter the pilgrims from listening to the Prophet ﷺ, Al-Walīd finally claimed that the Quran was 'transmitted magic' because its eloquence moved hearts so deeply that it separated a believer from the falsehood of his idolatrous relatives.
tafsirEn.74:25:
Denying Revelation: 'This Is Only the Word of a Mortal!'

📜 Contradicting his own earlier admission that it was neither the speech of man nor jinn, he publicly called it human speech.
tafsirEn.74:26:
The Warning of Saqar (The Scorching Fire of Hell, v.26–29).

📜 Allāh warns those who knowingly slander His Book with *Saqar*, one of the levels of Hellfire that consumes thoroughly.
tafsirEn.74:27:
The Unimaginable Severity of Saqar.

📜 Magnifies the awe and dread of the punishment prepared for arrogant deniers.
tafsirEn.74:28:
It Leaves Nothing Unconsumed and Spares Nothing.

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid & Qatādah: It consumes flesh, bone, and sinew, and whenever they are restored, the punishment begins anew without respite.
tafsirEn.74:29:
Scorching and Blackening the Skin (Lawwāhatun lil-Bashar).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Its intense heat darkens the skin from afar as a warning to humanity.
tafsirEn.74:31:
The Fourfold Wisdom Behind Appointing Angels and Naming Their Number.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah: Allāh explains why He made the keepers of Hell angels (whose strength none can resist) and specified their number (19): as a trial for the polytheists, so the People of the Book may gain certainty (finding the same number in their Scriptures), so the believers may increase in faith, and to expose those with hypocrisy in their hearts; *'And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him!'*
tafsirEn.74:38:
Individual Accountability: Every Soul Held in Pledge for Its Deeds (v.38–39).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Every soul is held accountable and bound by what it has earned of deeds, except the Companions of the Right.
tafsirEn.74:39:
The Deliverance of the Companions of the Right (Ashāb al-Yamīn).

📜 Through Allāh's grace and their sincere faith and righteous deeds, the people of the Right are freed from captivity to sin and admitted into Gardens.
tafsirEn.74:42:
The Dialogue Between Paradise and Hell: 'What Led You into Saqar?' (v.40–47).

📜 From their lofty Gardens, the believers ask the criminals what brought them into Hellfire, receiving a four-part confession that summarizes the causes of ruin.
tafsirEn.74:51:
Fleeing from a Lion (Al-Qaswarah).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: *Al-Qaswarah* means the lion (or archers hunting); instead of approaching the Quran that brings them life, they flee from it as if fleeing from death.
tafsirEn.111:2:
Why Verse 2 Was Revealed Refuting Abū Lahab's Boast About His Wealth.

📜 Account of Ibn Mas‘ūd & Ibn ‘Abbās (At-Tabarī): When the Prophet ﷺ warned his clan of the punishment of the Hereafter, Abū Lahab arrogantly boasted: 'If what my nephew says is true, I will ransom myself on Judgment Day with my wealth and my sons!' Allāh revealed: 'His wealth will not avail him, nor that which he gained!'
tafsirEn.111:3:
The Living Prophecy of Abū Lahab's End (Dhāta Lahab).

📜 Foretold ten years before Abū Lahab's death after Badr that he would die upon disbelief without ever accepting Islam—even outwardly—providing a permanent historical proof of the Quran's divine origin.
tafsirEn.111:4:
Why Verses 4–5 Were Revealed Regarding Umm Jamīl (The Carrier of Firewood).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās, Mujāhid & Qatādah: Abū Lahab's wife, **Arwā bint Harb (Umm Jamīl)**, used to gather bundles of thorny branches (*Al-Hatab*) at night to scatter along the Prophet's ﷺ path and fueled enmity among Quraysh through slander.
tafsirEn.111:5:
The Rope of Twisted Fiber Around Her Neck (Hablun min Masad).

📜 Exegesis of Sa‘īd ibn Al-Musayyib & ‘Urwah: Umm Jamīl wore a costly necklace and swore by Al-Lāt and Al-‘Uzzā to spend its value in hostility against Muhammad ﷺ; Allāh decreed for her neck in the Hereafter a collar of fiery twisted rope just like the rope with which she carried thorns.
tafsirEn.81:2:
When the Stars Fall and Lose Their Light (Inkadarat).

📜 On the Day of Resurrection, the stars scatter from their orbits and their light is extinguished.
tafsirEn.81:3:
When the Mountains Are Uprooted and Set in Motion.

📜 The towering mountains are lifted from the earth and turned into floating dust, leaving the earth a level plain.
tafsirEn.81:4:
When Ten-Month Pregnant Camels (Al-‘Ishār) Are Neglected.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: Among the Arabs, ten-month pregnant she-camels about to give birth were the most prized possession on earth; yet the terror of the Hour will make people abandon what they cherished most.
tafsirEn.81:5:
When the Wild Beasts Are Gathered Together (Hushirat).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Hadith of Abū Hurayrah (Sahīh Muslim #2582): All creatures, including wild animals, are assembled on Judgment Day so that absolute justice is settled among them—even the hornless sheep taking its right from the horned sheep—before Allāh turns the animals to dust.
tafsirEn.81:6:
When the Seas Are Set Ablaze (Sujjirat).

📜 Exegesis of ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib & Ibn ‘Abbās: Allāh turns the vast oceans of water into a single raging sea of fire on the Day of Resurrection.
tafsirEn.81:7:
When the Souls Are Paired (Zuwwijat).

📜 Exegesis of ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattāb & Ibn ‘Abbās: Every soul is reunited with its body and grouped with its counterparts in faith or disbelief—the righteous with the righteous in Paradise, and the wicked with the wicked.
tafsirEn.81:8:
When the Female Infant Buried Alive (Al-Maw'ūdah) Is Questioned (v.8–9).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah: Abolishes and condemns the pre-Islamic atrocity of burying newborn daughters alive out of fear of poverty or false shame; on Judgment Day, the innocent child herself is gently asked as a devastating rebuke to her killer.
tafsirEn.81:9:
'For What Sin Was She Killed?'

📜 If the innocent victim is questioned so that her oppressor is silenced in shame, how severe will be the reckoning of the murderer himself!
tafsirEn.81:10:
When the Scrolls of Deeds Are Laid Open (Nushirat).

📜 Every person's scroll of deeds, folded at death, is spread open before them on the Day of Resurrection.
tafsirEn.81:11:
When the Sky Is Stripped Away (Kushitat).

📜 The canopy of the sky is drawn back and folded away.
tafsirEn.81:12:
When Hellfire Is Set Blazing (Su‘‘irat).

📜 Hellfire is kindled to its fiercest heat for the arrogant transgressors.
tafsirEn.81:13:
When Paradise Is Brought Near to the Righteous (Uzlifat).

📜 Paradise is brought close and adorned for the Muttaqūn before they even enter it.
tafsirEn.81:14:
The Answer to the Twelve Signs: 'Every Soul Will Know What It Has Brought!'

📜 When these twelve cosmic events occur—six in the world and six in the Hereafter—every soul will see with certainty all the good and evil it has presented.
tafsirEn.81:15:
The Oath by the Retreating, Sweeping Stars (Al-Khunnas al-Jawār al-Kunnas, v.15–16).

📜 Exegesis of ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib & Ibn ‘Abbās: Allāh swears by the stars and planets that recede from sight by day (*Al-Khunnas*), travel in their orbits (*Al-Jawār*), and withdraw into their cosmic courses (*Al-Kunnas*) just as gazelles return to their shelters.
tafsirEn.81:18:
And by the Dawn as It Breathes Light (Tanaffas).

📜 Depicts the breaking of dawn as the morning gently breathing forth light and breeze after the stillness of night.
tafsirEn.81:19:
The Quran Transmitted by the Noble Angel Jibrīl (v.19–21).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Ash-Sha‘bī: The *'noble Messenger'* in verses 19–21 is **Angel Jibrīl (Gabriel)**, through whom Allāh sent down the Quran to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
tafsirEn.81:20:
Jibrīl's Mighty Power and Exalted Rank Before the Lord of the Throne.

📜 Describes Jibrīl's immense angelic strength and his honored station near Allāh, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.
tafsirEn.81:21:
Obeyed in the Heavens and Supremely Trustworthy (Amīn).

📜 Jibrīl is obeyed by the angelic hosts in the heavens and completely trustworthy in conveying the Revelation without adding or omitting a single letter.
tafsirEn.81:22:
Defense of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ (v.22–24).

📜 Shifting from the angelic messenger (Jibrīl) to the human Messenger (**Muhammad ﷺ**), Allāh reminds Quraysh—who knew his lifelong honesty—that their companion is of the soundest mind and highest wisdom.
tafsirEn.81:25:
Complete Purity of the Quran from Any Satanic Influence.

📜 Refutes the slander of the polytheists by affirming that the Quran is Pure Revelation brought by the purest Angel to the purest Messenger ﷺ.
tafsirEn.81:27:
A Universal Reminder for All the Worlds (v.27–28).

📜 The Quran is an open reminder and guidance for all mankind and jinn.
tafsirEn.81:29:
Why Verse 29 Was Revealed in Reply to Abū Jahl: Human Will Under Allāh's Sovereign Will.

📜 Account of Sulaymān ibn Mūsā & Qatādah (At-Tabarī & Ibn Kathīr): When verse 28 ('For whoever among you wills to go straight') was revealed, Abū Jahl arrogantly boasted: 'The matter is entirely in our hands! If we wish we will go straight, and if we do not wish we will not!' Allāh immediately revealed verse 29: 'And you do not will except that Allāh wills—Lord of the Worlds!'
tafsirEn.87:2:
Allāh's Perfect Creation and Proportioning (Khalaqa fa-Sawwā).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: Allāh created every living being and proportioned humanity with upright stature, balanced faculties, and harmony of form.
tafsirEn.87:3:
Who Decreed Every Measure and Guided Creation (Qaddara fa-Hadā).

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid & Ibn ‘Abbās: Allāh decreed the measure, lifespan, and provision of every creature, guided every living thing to what sustains it in life, and guided humanity by showing them the path of good and evil.
tafsirEn.87:4:
Who Brings Forth the Green Pasture (v.4–5).

📜 Allāh sends down rain to bring forth lush green vegetation of every kind to nourish flocks and humanity.
tafsirEn.87:5:
Then Turns It into Dark, Dry Stubble (Ghuthā'an Ahwā).

📜 Just as green vegetation dries and darkens at the end of its season, the fleeting life of this world gives way to the Resurrection.
tafsirEn.87:6:
When and Why Verse 6 Was Revealed: 'We Will Make You Recite, So You Shall Not Forget!'

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid, Qatādah & Al-Kalbi: Out of intense eagerness not to forget a single word, the Prophet ﷺ used to repeat the verses rapidly along with Jibrīl before Jibrīl finished reciting; Allāh reassured His Messenger ﷺ that He Himself guaranteed to preserve the Quran in his heart so he would never forget it.
tafsirEn.87:7:
Except What Allāh Wills: His Knowledge of the Open and the Hidden.

📜 Refers to verses whose recitation or ruling Allāh willed to abrogate in His wisdom, for He knows both public speech and the deepest secrets of the heart.
tafsirEn.87:8:
'And We Will Ease You Toward the Path of Ease (Al-Yusrā)!'

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Allāh promises to make easy for the Prophet ﷺ and his Ummah every path of good, the tolerant Law of Islam (*Ash-Sharī‘ah as-Samhah*), and the deeds that lead to Paradise.
tafsirEn.87:9:
Command to Remind With the Quran (Fa-dhakkir in Nafa‘at adh-Dhikrā).

📜 Instructs the Prophet ﷺ and every caller to Truth to keep reminding people with the Quran, for the reminder always benefits receptive hearts and establishes proof.
tafsirEn.87:10:
The Heart That Reveres Allāh Takes Heed.

📜 Whoever fears standing before his Lord welcomes admonition and hastens to purify his soul.
tafsirEn.87:11:
While the Most Wretched Turns Away in Arrogance (v.11–13).

📜 Only the one who chooses stubborn rebellion shuns the reminder, leading himself to the Great Fire.
tafsirEn.74:43:
First Cause of Ruin: 'We Were Not of Those Who Prayed!'

📜 Exegesis of Ibn Mas‘ūd & Ash-Shāfi‘ī: They neglected the first duty toward the Creator: establishing prayer and worshipping Allāh alone.
tafsirEn.74:44:
Second Cause of Ruin: 'Nor Did We Feed the Poor!'

📜 Along with abandoning Allāh's right (prayer), they abandoned the right of creation by withholding charity and compassion from the needy.
tafsirEn.74:45:
Third Cause: Indulging in Vain Mockery Against the Truth.

📜 They used to join those who engaged in falsehood and ridiculed the revelations of Allāh.
tafsirEn.74:46:
Fourth Cause: Denying the Day of Recompense (Yawm ad-Dīn).

📜 Because they denied the Resurrection and the Reckoning, they lived without moral restraint.
tafsirEn.74:47:
'Until the Certainty (Death) Came to Us!'

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī): *Al-Yaqīn* here means death, at which point what they used to deny became undeniable reality and the time for repentance expired.
tafsirEn.74:50:
Why Do They Turn Away from the Reminder Like Startled Wild Donkeys? (v.49–51).

📜 Likens the polytheists' blind flight from the Quran's guidance to wild zebras bolting in panic.
tafsirEn.74:52:
Why Verse 52 Was Revealed: Their Arrogant Demand for Personal Scrolls from Heaven.

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid & Qatādah: Certain leaders of Quraysh declared that they would not follow the Prophet ﷺ unless Jibrīl brought each of them a personal, unsealed scroll from Allāh addressed by name; Allāh exposed that their real motive was simply lack of fear of the Hereafter (v.53).
tafsirEn.74:56:
Allāh Is the Lord Worthy of Reverence and the Lord of Forgiveness (v.54–56).

📜 Hadith of Anas ibn Mālik (At-Tirmidhī #3328 & Ibn Mājah #4249): Concludes the surah affirming that human remembrance is encompassed by Allāh's Will, and that He alone is worthy of being revered and obeyed (Ahl at-Taqwā) and worthy to forgive all who turn to Him in repentance (Ahl al-Maghfirah).
tafsirEn.81:16:
The Travelling Stars Returning to Their Courses.

📜 Highlights the precision of the celestial bodies moving across the night sky by Allāh's command.
tafsirEn.81:17:
And by the Night as It Approaches and Departs (‘As‘as).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: In classical Arabic, *‘As‘asa* carries the dual meaning of the night as it darkens upon arrival and as its darkness recedes before dawn.
tafsirEn.81:23:
When the Prophet ﷺ Beheld Jibrīl on the Clear Horizon (Al-Ufuq al-Mubīn).

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah & Ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3232 & Muslim #177): The Prophet ﷺ saw Angel Jibrīl in his true angelic form—with six hundred wings filling the eastern horizon—at *Al-Abtah* in Makkah (and a second time near the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary during the Ascension).
tafsirEn.81:24:
He Does Not Withhold or Conceal a Single Word of the Revelation (Bi-Danīn).

📜 Unlike worldly fortune-tellers who hoard secrets for payment, the Prophet ﷺ generously and faithfully conveys every word of Allāh's guidance to humanity.
tafsirEn.81:26:
'So Where Are You Going?' (Fa-ayna Tadhhabūn).

📜 A piercing question to anyone who turns away from the Quran: where else can your hearts and minds go after the path of Truth has become so clear?
tafsirEn.81:28:
For Whoever Among You Wills to Take the Straight Path.

📜 Affirms human responsibility and choice in following the straight path of faith and righteousness.
tafsirEn.87:12:
He Who Will Enter the Great Fire (An-Nār al-Kubrā, v.12–13).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Al-Hasan Al-Basrī: While worldly fire is small and temporary, the Great Fire of Hell awaits the arrogant denier who neither dies therein to find rest from torment nor lives a life of comfort.
tafsirEn.87:13:
Neither Dying Therein Nor Living a Life of Ease.

📜 Hadith of Abū Sa‘īd Al-Khudrī (Sahīh Muslim #185): As for the permanent inhabitants of the Fire whom Allāh wills to remain therein, they neither die nor live, whereas monotheists who sinned are eventually brought out through intercession.
tafsirEn.87:14:
Success Belongs to Whoever Purifies Himself (Qad Aflaha man Tazakkā, v.14–15).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās, ‘Atā' & Qatādah: Eternal triumph belongs to the believer who purifies his soul from polytheism and base traits (and gives charity such as Zakāt al-Fitr), remembers the Name of his Lord, and establishes prayer.
tafsirEn.87:15:
Remembering the Name of His Lord and Praying (Fa-dhakara Isma Rabbihi fa-Sallā).

📜 Unites inward remembrance of Allāh's majesty with outward submission in the five daily prayers.
tafsirEn.87:16:
Preferring the Fleeting World Over the Hereafter (v.16–17).

📜 Statement of Ibn Mas‘ūd: Ibn Mas‘ūd explained that people naturally incline toward the immediate pleasures of this world unless guided by certainty that the Hereafter is infinitely better in quality and everlasting in duration.
tafsirEn.87:17:
While the Hereafter Is Better and More Enduring (Khayrun wa Abqā).

📜 Hadith of Al-Mustawrid (Sahīh Muslim #2858): The Prophet ﷺ said that this world compared to the Hereafter is no more than what clings to one's finger when dipped into the vast ocean.
tafsirEn.87:18:
Confirmed in the Earlier Scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā (v.18–19).

📜 Hadith of Abū Dharr (Ibn Hibbān) & Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: These foundational truths—that purification, remembrance, and prayer bring salvation, and that the Hereafter is better and everlasting—were inscribed in the ancient Scrolls revealed to Prophets Ibrāhīm and Mūsā (peace be upon them).
tafsirEn.87:19:
The Scrolls of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā (Suhuf Ibrāhīm wa Mūsā).

📜 Demonstrates the complete harmony of all divine revelations across history.
tafsirEn.92:2:
By the Day When It Appears in Brightness (Tajallā, v.2–3).

📜 Following the oath by the night, Allāh swears by the day as its light dispels darkness and by Him Who created male and female.
tafsirEn.92:3:
And by He Who Created the Male and the Female.

📜 Hadith of Abū Ad-Dardā' (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4944 & Muslim #824): Just as night and day and male and female are paired opposites, human striving is divided into two contrasting paths.
tafsirEn.92:4:
'Indeed, Your Efforts Are Diverse!' (Inna Sa‘yakum la-Shattā).

📜 Hadith of Abū Mālik Al-Ash‘arī (Sahīh Muslim #223): Every person wakes up in the morning and sells his soul—either freeing it through obedience to Allāh or ruining it through disobedience.
tafsirEn.92:5:
Why Verses 5–7 Were Revealed Regarding Abū Bakr As-Siddīq's Generosity.

📜 Hadith of ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4949 & Muslim #2647) & Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: As for him who gives his wealth in charity, fears Allāh, and believes in the best reward (Al-Husnā—monotheism and Paradise), Allāh facilitates for him every path of ease and goodness.
tafsirEn.92:6:
And Believes in the Best Reward (Wa Saddaqa bil-Husnā).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: *Al-Husnā* encompasses testifying to *Lā ilāha illā Allāh* and certainty in Allāh's promised reward in this life and the Hereafter.
tafsirEn.92:7:
'We Will Ease Him Toward Ease (Al-Yusrā)!'

📜 When the companions asked if they should rely on decree and abandon action, the Prophet ﷺ recited these verses and replied: 'Work and strive, for everyone is facilitated toward that for which he was created!' (Al-Bukhārī #4949).
tafsirEn.92:8:
The Path of Miserliness and Arrogant Self-Sufficiency (v.8–10).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Contrasts the generous believer with the miser (such as Umayyah ibn Khalaf) who withholds Allāh's right, deems himself independent of his Lord's mercy, and denies the hereafter.
tafsirEn.92:9:
And Denies the Best Reward (Wa Kadhdhaba bil-Husnā).

📜 Rejecting both pure faith and the promise of recompense.
tafsirEn.92:10:
Facilitated Toward Hardship and Ruin (Lil-‘Usrā).

📜 Because he chose stubbornness and greed, the path of evil becomes his chosen course.
tafsirEn.92:11:
His Hoarded Wealth Will Not Avail Him When He Perishes (Taraddā).

📜 When he falls into his grave and into Hellfire, all the wealth he hoarded will be of no benefit.
tafsirEn.92:12:
Upon Allāh Rests the Clarification of Guidance (v.12–13).

📜 Exegesis of Qatādah: Allāh has made clear the path of guidance and the path of ruin, and to Him alone belong both the Hereafter and this world.
tafsirEn.92:13:
And Indeed, to Us Belong the Hereafter and the First Life.

📜 Whoever seeks the good of either world must seek it from Allāh alone.
tafsirEn.92:15:
None Shall Enter It Permanently Except the Most Wretched (Al-Ashqā).

📜 Refers to the obstinate disbeliever who rejected the truth.
tafsirEn.92:16:
Who Denied the Truth and Turned Away.

📜 Denied the Quran in his heart and turned away from obedience in his actions.
tafsirEn.92:17:
When and Why Verses 17–21 Were Revealed in Honor of Abū Bakr As-Siddīq.

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās, ‘Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr & Ibn Mas‘ūd (At-Tabarī, Al-Bazzār & Ibn Hishām): The exegetes are unanimous that these verses—'And the most righteous (Al-Atqā) shall be kept far away from it'—were revealed regarding **Abū Bakr As-Siddīq** (may Allāh be pleased with him).
tafsirEn.92:18:
'Who Gives His Wealth to Purify Himself (Yatazakkā).'

📜 When Abū Bakr purchased and freed seven weak, tortured Muslims in Makkah (including **Bilāl** and ‘Āmir ibn Fuhayrah), his father Abū Quhāfah said: 'O my son, if you freed strong men they could protect you!' Abū Bakr replied that he sought only Allāh's reward.
tafsirEn.92:19:
Not Repaying Any Worldly Favor to Anyone.

📜 Allāh testified that none of those freed by Abū Bakr owed him any prior worldly favor that he was repaying.
tafsirEn.92:20:
'Except Seeking the Countenance of His Lord, the Most High!'

📜 His charity was 100% pure sincerity (*Ikhlās*) seeking only the Face of Allāh.
tafsirEn.92:21:
'And He Will Surely Be Well-Pleased!' (Wa la-Sawfa Yardā).

📜 Allāh's eternal promise to satisfy Abū Bakr As-Siddīq and every sincere believer who follows his example with supreme honor in Paradise.
tafsirEn.89:2:
And by the Ten Nights (Wa Layālin ‘Ashr, v.2–5).

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #969 & Musnad Ahmad): The Ten Nights are the first ten days of **Dhū al-Hijjah**, regarding which the Prophet ﷺ said: 'There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allāh than these ten days!'
tafsirEn.89:3:
And by the Even and the Odd (Wash-Shaf‘i wal-Watr).

📜 Hadith of ‘Imrān ibn Husayn & Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Encompasses all of creation (which is either even or odd), the Day of Sacrifice (the 10th, Even) and the Day of ‘Arafah (the 9th, Odd), and Allāh Who is One (*Witr*) while creation is paired (*Shaf‘*).
tafsirEn.89:4:
And by the Night When It Passes On (Yasr).

📜 Swearing by the movement of the night as it departs before the dawn.
tafsirEn.89:5:
'Is There Not in That a Sufficient Oath for Those of Understanding (Dhī Hijr)?'

📜 *Hijr* means sound intellect because it restrains (*Yahjur*) its owner from evil and ignorance.
tafsirEn.89:6:
The Lesson of ‘Ād and Iram of the Lofty Pillars (v.6–8).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: Reminds Quraysh how Allāh dealt with the ancient tribe of **‘Ād** (the people of Prophet Hūd), the tribe of Iram famed for their giant stature and towering stone pillars.
tafsirEn.89:7:
Iram of the Lofty Pillars (Dhāt al-‘Imād).

📜 Despite their architectural power and physical strength, they could not withstand Allāh's decree when they rejected His Messenger.
tafsirEn.89:8:
'The Like of Whom Had Never Been Created in the Lands!'

📜 Highlights the unmatched strength given to ‘Ād in their era.
tafsirEn.89:9:
And Thamūd Who Carved Out the Rocks in the Valley (Al-Qurā).

📜 The people of Prophet Sālih who hewed fortified palaces out of the mountains in Wādī al-Qurā (Al-Hijr).
tafsirEn.89:10:
And Pharaoh, Owner of the Stakes (Dhī al-Awtād, v.10–14).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah: Refers to Pharaoh's vast armies, tent-stakes, and instruments with which he tortured believers (such as his believing wife **Āsiyah**).
tafsirEn.89:11:
Who Transgressed All Bounds in the Lands (v.11–12).

📜 All three powers—‘Ād, Thamūd, and Pharaoh—rebelled against Allāh and spread tyranny.
tafsirEn.89:12:
And Multiplied Corruption Therein.

📜 Filled the earth with oppression and disbelief.
tafsirEn.89:13:
So Your Lord Poured Upon Them a Scourge of Punishment.

📜 Allāh sent down His decisive retribution upon each of them.
tafsirEn.89:14:
'Indeed, Your Lord Is Ever Watchful (La-bil-Mirsād)!'

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Nothing escapes Allāh's sight; He watches the deeds of every oppressor and repays each according to justice.
tafsirEn.89:15:
The True Meaning of Wealth and Trial (v.15–16).

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid & Ibn ‘Abbās: Refutes the materialistic illusion of those (like Umayyah ibn Khalaf and Ubayy ibn Khalaf) who think abundant wealth means Allāh honors them and restricted provision means Allāh humiliates them; rather, both are a test!
tafsirEn.89:16:
When Provision Is Measured Out as a Trial.

📜 Allāh tests the wealthy with gratitude and charity, and tests the poor with patience and trust in Him.
tafsirEn.89:17:
Why Verses 17–20 Were Revealed: Neglecting the Orphan and the Poor.

📜 Exegesis of Muqātil & Ibn ‘Abbās: Revealed exposing how the wealthy of Quraysh failed the test of wealth by withholding the inheritance of orphans (such as Qudāmah ibn Maz‘ūn in his youth) and failing to encourage feeding the needy.
tafsirEn.89:18:
And You Do Not Urge One Another to Feed the Poor.

📜 Shows that true faith requires both personal charity and mutual encouragement to care for the poor.
tafsirEn.89:19:
Devouring Inheritance Greedily (Aklan Lammā, v.19–20).

📜 Condemns pre-Islamic greed in consuming the shares of women and orphans alongside their own.
tafsirEn.89:20:
And Loving Wealth with an Excessive, Consuming Love (Hubban Jammā).

📜 Anordinate attachment to wealth that blinds the heart to the Hereafter.
tafsirEn.89:21:
When the Earth Is Pounded to Powder (Dakkan Dakkā, v.21–24).

📜 Depicts the convulsion of the Earth on the Day of Resurrection when all mountains and structures are leveled.
tafsirEn.89:22:
And Your Lord Comes, and the Angels Rank Upon Rank (Saffan Saffā).

📜 Allāh comes to judge His servants in a manner befitting His Majesty, while the angels descend in vast ranks.
tafsirEn.89:24:
He Will Say: 'Oh, I Wish I Had Sent Ahead Good for My Eternal Life (Li-Hayātī)!'

📜 Realizing that the true, everlasting life is the life of the Hereafter.
tafsirEn.89:25:
The Unmatched Punishment of the Defiant (v.25–26).

📜 None punishes as severely as Allāh punishes the arrogant criminal on that Day.
tafsirEn.89:26:
And None Binds as He Binds.

📜 Complete justice upon those who oppressed and denied.
tafsirEn.89:27:
The Call to the Tranquil, Reassured Soul (Yā Ayyatuhā an-Nafs al-Mutma'innah, v.27–30).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās, Sa‘īd ibn Jubayr & Qatādah: Revealed regarding the believing soul reassured by Allāh's promise (exemplified by companions like **‘Uthmān ibn ‘Affān**, **Hamzah**, and **Khubayb ibn ‘Adī**), who is told at death and on Resurrection Day: 'O tranquil soul, return to your Lord well-pleased and pleasing to Him!'
tafsirEn.89:28:
'Return to Your Lord, Well-Pleased and Pleasing to Him (Rādiyatan Mardiyyah)!'

📜 Pleased with Allāh's decree and reward, and having earned Allāh's eternal pleasure.
tafsirEn.89:29:
'So Enter Among My Righteous Servants!'

📜 Joined with the company of Prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous.
tafsirEn.89:30:
'And Enter My Paradise!'

📜 The supreme honor of entering Allāh's eternal Abode of Peace.
tafsirEn.93:2:
And by the Night When It Grows Still and Calm (Idhā Sajā).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: Swears by the morning light and the tranquil stillness of the night that Allāh never forsook His Messenger ﷺ.
tafsirEn.93:4:
'And the Hereafter Is Surely Better for You Than the First Life!'

📜 Hadith of Ibn Mas‘ūd & Ibn ‘Abbās: Every step forward and the eternal honor of the Hereafter are far greater for the Prophet ﷺ than anything in this fleeting world.
tafsirEn.93:5:
'And Your Lord Is Going to Give You, and You Will Be Satisfied!' (Wa la-Sawfa Yu‘tīka Rabbuka fa-Tardā).

📜 Hadith of ‘Abdullāh ibn ‘Amr (Sahīh Muslim #202) & Ibn ‘Abbās: Ibn ‘Abbās called this the most hopeful verse in the Quran because the Prophet ﷺ declared that he will not be satisfied while a single one of his true followers remains in the Fire—pointing to his Grand Intercession (*Ash-Shafā‘ah*) on Judgment Day.
tafsirEn.93:6:
Remembering Allāh's Care During the Prophet's ﷺ Orphanhood (v.6–8).

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid & Qatādah: Reminds the Prophet ﷺ how his father ‘Abdullāh died before his birth and his mother Āminah died when he was six, yet Allāh sheltered him through his grandfather ‘Abd al-Muttalib and his uncle Abū Tālib.
tafsirEn.93:7:
'And He Found You Unaware of the Scripture, So He Guided You!'

📜 Before revelation (as stated in Surah 42:52), the Prophet ﷺ did not know the details of the Book, and Allāh guided him by revealing the Quran.
tafsirEn.93:8:
'And He Found You in Need, So He Made You Self-Sufficient!'

📜 Enriched his heart with contentment and blessed his livelihood through Khadījah's trade and divine provision.
tafsirEn.93:9:
Three Practical Duties of Gratitude: Honoring the Orphan (v.9–11).

📜 Commands the believer to treat orphans with tenderness and protect their rights.
tafsirEn.93:10:
'And as for the Petitioner (As-Sā'il), Do Not Repel Him!'

📜 Whether someone asks for charity or asks for religious knowledge, respond with kindness and generosity.
tafsirEn.93:11:
'And as for the Favor of Your Lord, Proclaim It!' (Fa-Haddith).

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid & Qatādah: Speaking of Allāh's blessings—especially the blessing of Islam and the Quran—out of humble gratitude is an act of worship.
tafsirEn.94:2:
Removing the Heavy Burden (Wa Wada‘nā ‘anka Wizrak, v.2–3).

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid & Qatādah: Allāh relieved the Prophet ﷺ of the heavy anxiety he felt for his people's guidance and forgave him.
tafsirEn.94:3:
'Which Had Weighed Upon Your Back.'

📜 Highlights the immense weight of responsibility that Allāh lightened through His support.
tafsirEn.94:5:
The Double Promise: 'For Indeed, With Hardship Comes Ease!' (v.5–6).

📜 Statement of ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattāb & Ibn Mas‘ūd (Al-Hākim & Malik): In Arabic grammar, *Al-‘Usr* (the hardship) is definite and singular in both verses, while *Yusran* (ease) is indefinite and repeated—leading the Prophet ﷺ and his companions to proclaim: 'One hardship can never overcome two eases!'
tafsirEn.94:6:
'Indeed, With Hardship Comes Ease!'

📜 Reaffirms that relief is already bound to every trial.
tafsirEn.94:7:
Devotion After Completing Worldly Tasks (Fa-idhā Faraghta fansab, v.7–8).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn Mas‘ūd & Ibn ‘Abbās: Whenever you finish your worldly duties or obligatory prayer, strive earnestly in supplication and night devotion.
tafsirEn.94:8:
'And to Your Lord Direct Your Longing!' (Farghab).

📜 Place all your hope, supplication, and longing in Allāh alone.
tafsirEn.103:2:
Humanity Is in Loss Except Those Who Fulfill Four Pillars (v.2–3).

📜 Every moment of passing time (*Al-‘Asr*) diminishes human lifespan unless invested in eternal good.
tafsirEn.103:3:
The Four Pillars of Salvation: Faith, Righteous Deeds, Truth, and Patience.

📜 Statement of Imam Ash-Shāfi‘ī: Unites personal perfection (faith and righteous deeds) with collective responsibility (enjoining Truth and enjoining Patience upon one another).
tafsirEn.100:2:
And the Chargers Striking Sparks of Fire (Fal-Mūriyāti Qadhā, v.2–5).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & ‘Alī: Swears by the horses charging in Allāh's cause whose hooves strike sparks against the rocks.
tafsirEn.100:3:
Making Raids at Dawn (Fal-Mughīrāti Subhā).

📜 Charging forth at daybreak.
tafsirEn.100:4:
Raising Clouds of Dust Thereby (Fa-Atharna bihi Naq‘ā).

📜 Stirring up dust in the valley.
tafsirEn.100:5:
Penetrating the Center of the Gathering (Fa-Wasatna bihi Jam‘ā).

📜 Completing thefive-part oath leading to the main truth in verse 6.
tafsirEn.100:6:
'Indeed, Man Is Ungrateful to His Lord (La-Kanūd)!' (v.6–8).

📜 Hadith of Al-Hasan Al-Basrī & Ibn ‘Abbās: *Al-Kanūd* is the one who counts misfortunes and forgets the countless blessings of his Lord.
tafsirEn.100:7:
'And Indeed, He Is a Witness to That Himself!'

📜 Man's own conscience and actions testify to his ingratitude when left to his desires.
tafsirEn.100:8:
'And Indeed, He Is Intense in His Love of Wealth (Al-Khayr)!'

📜 Here *Al-Khayr* refers to worldly wealth; man loves it intensely unless guided by faith to spend it in charity.
tafsirEn.100:9:
Awakening to the Resurrection and the Reckoning (v.9–11).

📜 Calls humanity to remember the Day when what is in the graves is scattered forth and the secrets hidden in chests are brought to light before their All-Aware Lord.
tafsirEn.100:10:
And That Which Is Within the Breasts Is Brought to Light.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah: Every secret intention, belief, and motive concealed inside human hearts during worldly life will be exposed and judged on the Day of Resurrection.
tafsirEn.100:11:
'Indeed, Their Lord That Day Is Fully Aware of Them!'

📜 Allāh has always been fully aware of every deed, and on that Day He repays them in full according to His complete knowledge.
tafsirEn.108:2:
'So Pray to Your Lord and Sacrifice!' (Fa-Salli li-Rabbika wanhar).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās, ‘Atā' & Qatādah: Unlike the polytheists who prayed and sacrificed to idols, make your prayer and your sacrificial offering purely and exclusively for Allāh, your Lord.
tafsirEn.108:3:
Why Verse 3 Was Revealed: 'Indeed, Your Enemy Is the One Cut Off (Al-Abtar)!'

📜 Account of Ibn ‘Abbās (Al-Bazzār & At-Tabarī): Revealed regarding Al-‘Ās ibn Wā'il (or ‘Uqbah ibn Abī Mu‘ayt and Abū Lahab) who claimed that the Prophet's ﷺ memory would die out after the passing of his young son Al-Qāsim; Allāh cut off his enemies' legacy while exalting the Prophet's ﷺ name until the end of time.
tafsirEn.102:2:
'Until You Visit the Graves!'

📜 Hadith of ‘Abdullāh ibn Ash-Shikhkhīr (Sahīh Muslim #2958) & Qatādah: Rivalry in worldly wealth and tribal numbers distracts the heedless until death overtakes them and they enter their graves—and the rival clans even boasted over the number of their dead buried in the cemeteries.
tafsirEn.102:3:
'No! You Are Going to Know!' (v.3–4).

📜 Statement of ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib & Ibn ‘Abbās: The first warning addresses the moment of death and the punishment of the grave, while the second addresses the Day of Resurrection.
tafsirEn.102:4:
'Then No! You Are Going to Know!'

📜 Reaffirms the certainty of the Reckoning when they stand before their Lord.
tafsirEn.102:5:
'No! If You Only Knew with Knowledge of Certainty (‘Ilm al-Yaqīn)!'

📜 If your hearts possessed true certainty regarding the Hereafter, worldly rivalry would never have distracted you from obedience to Allāh.
tafsirEn.102:6:
'You Will Surely See the Hellfire!' (v.6–7).

📜 Announces that the creation will behold the Blazing Fire with their own eyes on the Day of Judgment.
tafsirEn.102:7:
'Then You Will Surely See It with the Eye of Certainty (‘Ayn al-Yaqīn)!'

📜 Knowledge of the unseen becomes direct visual witnessing on the Day of Resurrection.
tafsirEn.102:8:
Questioning About the Blessings (An-Na‘īm) on Judgment Day.

📜 Hadith of Abū Hurayrah (Sahīh Muslim #2038 & At-Tirmidhī #2369): When the Prophet ﷺ went out at midday with Abū Bakr and ‘Umar out of hunger and an Ansārī companion hosted them with shade, fresh dates, meat, and cool water, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, this is part of the blessing (An-Na‘īm) about which you will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection—whether you were grateful to Allāh for it!'
tafsirEn.107:2:
Why Verses 2–3 Were Revealed: Harshly Repelling the Orphan.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Muqātil: Revealed regarding miserly Quraishi chiefs (such as Abū Jahl, who was guardian to an orphan boy and drove him away when he came asking for his own property, or Al-‘Ās ibn Wā'il) whose denial of the Day of Judgment made their hearts cruel toward the weak.
tafsirEn.107:3:
And Does Not Encourage the Feeding of the Poor.

📜 Neither feeds the needy from his own wealth nor urges others to show mercy to the poor.
tafsirEn.107:4:
'So Woe to Those Who Pray—Who Are Heedless of Their Prayer!' (v.4–5).

📜 Hadith of Sa‘d ibn Abī Waqqās & Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās (At-Tabarī): Ibn ‘Abbās praised Allāh that He said *'heedless of their prayer'* (`‘an salātihim`) rather than *'in their prayer'*: it refers to those who carelessly delay prayer beyond its prescribed time or neglect it altogether when alone.
tafsirEn.107:5:
Who Are Neglectful of Their Prayer's Time and Essence.

📜 Performing it without mindfulness, humility, or respect for its appointed hours.
tafsirEn.107:6:
'Those Who Make a Show of Their Deeds (Yurā'ūn)!'

📜 Praying and acting only to be seen and praised by people rather than seeking Allāh's pleasure.
tafsirEn.107:7:
And Withhold Even Small Kindnesses (Al-Mā‘ūn).

📜 Exegesis of ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, Ibn Mas‘ūd & Ibn ‘Abbās: Encompasses both withholding obligatory Zakāt and refusing to lend everyday household necessities (such as a bucket, pot, axe, or water) to neighbors.
tafsirEn.109:2:
'I Do Not Worship What You Worship!'

📜 Complete disavowal of every idol and false deity worshipped besides Allāh.
tafsirEn.109:3:
'Nor Are You Worshippers of What I Worship!'

📜 So long as they associate partners with Allāh, their worship is rejected because Allāh accepts only pure monotheism.
tafsirEn.109:4:
'Nor Will I Ever Be a Worshipper of What You Worshipped!' (v.4–5).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Al-Bukhārī: Negates worship of idols both in the present and in the future, shutting the door forever against the Quraishi offer of alternating worship year by year.
tafsirEn.109:5:
Reaffirming Complete Separation Between Pure Tawhīd and Shirk.

📜 Declares that true worship of Allāh cannot coexist with polytheism.
tafsirEn.109:6:
'For You Is Your Religion, and for Me Is My Religion!'

📜 Hadith of Farwah ibn Nawfal (Abū Dāwūd #5055): The Prophet ﷺ instructed his companions to recite this surah upon going to sleep, for it is a declaration of complete freedom from polytheism (*Barā'atun mina ash-Shirk*).
tafsirEn.105:2:
'Did He Not Make Their Treacherous Plan Go Astray?'

📜 Abrahah's plot to demolish the Sacred Ka‘bah and divert the Arabs' pilgrimage to his cathedral in Yemen ended in total failure.
tafsirEn.105:3:
Flocks of Birds Sent Against Abrahah's Army (Tayran Abābīl, v.3–4).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Sa‘īd ibn Jubayr: Allāh sent wave after wave of birds from the direction of the sea, each carrying three small stones of baked clay (*Sijjīl*)—one in its beak and two in its claws.
tafsirEn.105:4:
Striking Them with Stones of Hardened Clay (Hijāratin min Sijjīl).

📜 Whoever was struck by one of these stones perished on the spot.
tafsirEn.105:5:
'And He Made Them Like Eaten Straw ('Asfin Ma'kūl)!'

📜 Their mighty army was left crushed and hollow like chewed stalks of grain.
tafsirEn.113:2:
'From the Evil of That Which He Created.'

📜 Seeking Allāh's protection from the harm of every wicked creature among humans, jinn, and beasts.
tafsirEn.113:3:
'And From the Evil of the Darkening Night When It Settles (Ghāsiqin idhā Waqab).'

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah (At-Tirmidhī #3366) & Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Encompasses the darkness of the night when harmful creatures and evil-doers emerge, as well as the moon when it is eclipsed.
tafsirEn.113:4:
'And From the Evil of the Blowers in Knots (An-Naffāthāti fī al-‘Uqad).'

📜 Refers to sorcerers and witches who tie knots and blow incantations upon them to cause harm.
tafsirEn.113:5:
'And From the Evil of an Envier When He Envies (Hāsidin idhā Hasad).'

📜 Seeking refuge in Allāh from the destructive malice of the envious person who resents the blessings Allāh bestows upon His servants.
tafsirEn.114:2:
'The Sovereign of Mankind, the God of Mankind' (v.2–3).

📜 Invokes Allāh by His Lordship (*Rabb*), His absolute Kingship (*Malik*), and His exclusive Divinity (*Ilāh*)—showing the supreme danger of the unseen whisperer.
tafsirEn.114:3:
'The God of Mankind (Ilāh an-Nās).'

📜 The only One worthy of worship and refuge.
tafsirEn.114:4:
'From the Evil of the Retreating Whisperer (Al-Waswās al-Khannās).'

📜 Statement of Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī): Satan perches near the human heart: when the servant becomes heedless, he whispers evil (*Waswasa*), and as soon as the servant remembers Allāh, he shrinks back and retreats (*Khanasa*).
tafsirEn.114:5:
'Who Whispers into the Breasts of Mankind.'

📜 Casting doubts, temptations, and anxieties into the hearts of the heedless.
tafsirEn.114:6:
'From Among the Jinn and Mankind.'

📜 Warns against both unseen devils among the jinn and human companions who whisper evil and beautify sin.
tafsirEn.112:2:
'Allāh, the Eternal Refuge (As-Samad)!'

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & ‘Ikrimah: *As-Samad* is the Master Whose sovereignty and perfection are complete, upon Whom all creation depends for all their needs while He depends on none.
tafsirEn.112:3:
'He Neither Begets Nor Is Born!'

📜 Hadith Qudsī of Abū Hurayrah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4974): Refutes every false claim of polytheists and deviated sects who attributed offspring or parentage to Allāh.
tafsirEn.112:4:
'Nor Is There to Him Any Equivalent (Kufuwan Ahad)!'

📜 Nothing in existence resembles Him in His Essence, Names, Attributes, or Actions.
tafsirEn.53:2:
Allāh's Oath That Muhammad ﷺ Never Strayed Nor Erred (v.2–4).

📜 Swearing by the star as it sets, Allāh testifies that His Messenger ﷺ never deviated from the path of Truth.
tafsirEn.53:3:
'Nor Does He Speak from His Own Inclination (Al-Hawā)!'

📜 Hadith of ‘Abdullāh ibn ‘Amr (Abū Dāwūd #3646): Everything the Prophet ﷺ conveys of the Quran and religious guidance is free from personal whim.
tafsirEn.53:4:
'It Is Nothing Less Than a Revelation Revealed!'

📜 Pure divine revelation sent down to him from the Lord of the Worlds.
tafsirEn.53:5:
'Taught to Him by One Intense in Strength (Jibrīl)!' (v.5–7).

📜 Hadith of Ibn Mas‘ūd & ‘Ā'ishah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4856 & Muslim #174): Refers to **Angel Jibrīl (Gabriel)**, endowed with immense strength and beauty.
tafsirEn.53:6:
Possessor of Soundness and Majesty; and He Rose to His True Form (Fastawā).

📜 Jibrīl appeared in his true angelic form created by Allāh.
tafsirEn.53:7:
'While He Was in the Highest Part of the Horizon.'

📜 Standing on the highest eastern horizon, filling the sky with his six hundred wings.
tafsirEn.53:8:
'Then He Approached and Came Closer—About Two Bow-Lengths or Nearer' (v.8–10).

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah & Ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Muslim #174 & #177): Jibrīl drew near to the Prophet ﷺ to deliver Allāh's revelation.
tafsirEn.53:9:
'And Was at a Distance of Two Bow-Lengths (Qāba Qawsayn) or Nearer.'

📜 Expresses the closeness of Angel Jibrīl when conveying the revelation.
tafsirEn.53:10:
'And He Revealed to His Servant What He Revealed!'

📜 Allāh revealed through Jibrīl to His servant Muhammad ﷺ the majestic message.
tafsirEn.53:11:
'The Heart Did Not Lie About What It Saw!' (v.11–12).

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Muslim #176): Confirms the truth of what the Prophet ﷺ witnessed during his Night Ascension (*Al-Mi‘rāj*).
tafsirEn.53:12:
'So Will You Dispute with Him Over What He Saw?'

📜 Rebukes the polytheists of Quraysh who disputed the Prophet's ﷺ account of the Night Journey and Ascension.
tafsirEn.53:13:
The Second Vision at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntahā, v.13–18).

📜 Hadith of Ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Muslim #173 & Al-Bukhārī #3234): The Prophet ﷺ saw Jibrīl in his true form a second time during the Night of *Al-Mi‘rāj* at *Sidrat al-Muntahā* in the seventh heaven, where the instructions from the earth ascend and the decrees of heaven descend.
tafsirEn.53:14:
'Near the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntahā).'

📜 The furthest point reached by creation's knowledge, beyond which none knows what lies except Allāh.
tafsirEn.53:15:
'Near It Is the Garden of Abode (Jannat al-Ma'wā).'

📜 The Eternal Paradise where the souls of the righteous and martyrs abide.
tafsirEn.53:16:
'When There Covered the Lote Tree That Which Covered It!'

📜 Covered by indescribable divine light, angels, and golden butterflies.
tafsirEn.53:17:
The Prophet's ﷺ Supreme Etiquette: 'The Sight Did Not Swerve, Nor Did It Transgress!'

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: In the highest heaven, the Prophet ﷺ neither turned his gaze left or right nor looked beyond what he was commanded to behold.
tafsirEn.53:18:
'He Certainly Saw of the Greatest Signs of His Lord!'

📜 Witnessing the wonders of the heavens, Paradise, and the Lote Tree on the Night of Ascension.
tafsirEn.53:20:
'And Manāt, the Third—the Other One?'

📜 Asks how inanimate stones could possess any divinity or intercession.
tafsirEn.53:21:
'Is the Male for You and for Him the Female?' (v.21–22).

📜 Condemns the contradiction of the idolaters who hated having daughters yet claimed the angels were 'Allāh's daughters'.
tafsirEn.53:22:
'That, Then, Would Be an Unjust Division (Qismatun Dīzā)!'

📜 Exposes the absurdity of their fabricated beliefs.
tafsirEn.53:23:
'They Are Nothing But Names You and Your Forefathers Have Invented!'

📜 Idols are mere hollow names devoid of any authority from Allāh.
tafsirEn.53:31:
Why Verses 31–32 Were Revealed: Recompensing Evil and Rewarding the Doers of Good.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: To Allāh belongs all that is in the heavens and earth, so He may requite those who do evil and reward with Paradise those who avoid the major sins and indecencies except for minor, unintended slips (Al-Lamam) followed by repentance.
tafsirEn.53:32:
Avoiding Major Sins & Prohibition of Self-Praise (Falā Tuzakkū Anfusakum).

📜 Hadith of Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn ‘Atā' (Sahīh Muslim #2142): Commands humility: do not boast of your own purity, for Allāh knows best who truly fears Him since the moment He created you from the earth and while you were fetuses in your mothers' wombs.
tafsirEn.53:36:
When and Why Verses 33–41 Were Revealed: The Scrolls of Mūsā and Ibrāhīm.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: Revealed when a man (said to be Al-Walīd ibn Al-Mughīrah or ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Affān's foster brother before repentance) paid another man a sum of money to 'carry his sins on Judgment Day' and then stopped giving the rest! Allāh revealed that in the Scriptures of Mūsā and Ibrāhīm—who faithfully fulfilled every command—no soul shall ever bear the burden of another (v.38).
tafsirEn.53:37:
'And of Ibrāhīm, Who Fulfilled All His Obligations (Alladhī Waffā)!'

📜 Praises Prophet Ibrāhīm for fulfilling every trial and commandment entrusted to him by his Lord.
tafsirEn.53:38:
Universal Justice: 'That No Bearer of Burdens Shall Bear the Burden of Another!'

📜 Every soul is accountable only for its own deeds.
tafsirEn.53:39:
'And That There Is Not for Man Except That for Which He Strives!'

📜 Faith and salvation are earned through sincere personal striving rather than tribal lineage or false ransoms.
tafsirEn.53:40:
'And That His Striving Will Surely Be Seen!' (v.40–41).

📜 Every good deed is preserved by Allāh, displayed in full on the Day of Resurrection, and rewarded with the fullest recompense.
tafsirEn.53:41:
'Then He Will Be Recompensed for It with the Fullest Recompense!'

📜 Multiplied from tenfold to seven hundredfold and beyond by Allāh's generosity.
tafsirEn.53:42:
'And That to Your Lord Is the Final Goal (Al-Muntahā)!'

📜 All creation, all affairs, and all journeys end before Allāh alone.
tafsirEn.53:43:
'And That It Is He Who Makes One Laugh and Weep!'

📜 Allāh alone creates the causes of joy and sorrow, life and death (v.44), and wealth and sufficiency (v.48).
tafsirEn.53:50:
The Destruction of the First ‘Ād, Thamūd, and the People of Nūh (v.50–54).

📜 Reminds the deniers of how Allāh destroyed the mighty nations of old when they persisted in rebellion.
tafsirEn.53:57:
The Approaching Hour & the First Collective Prostration of Recitation (v.57–62).

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās & Ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #1070 & #4862): Surah An-Najm was the first surah containing a prostration of recitation (*Sajdah*) that the Prophet ﷺ recited publicly in the Sanctuary of Makkah; so overpowering was its final call—'So prostrate to Allāh and worship Him!'—that the Muslims, the polytheists, the jinn, and all mankind present prostrated together!
tafsirEn.80:2:
When and Why Verses 1–10 Were Revealed Regarding ‘Abdullāh ibn Umm Maktūm.

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah & Anas (At-Tirmidhī #3331 & Al-Muwatta'): While the Prophet ﷺ was earnestly calling top Quraishi leaders (such as ‘Utbah ibn Rabī‘ah and Abū Jahl) hoping their Islam would protect the weak believers, the blind companion **‘Abdullāh ibn Umm Maktūm** came asking: 'O Messenger of Allāh, teach me from what Allāh has taught you!' Allāh revealed these verses elevating the sincere seeker of purity over the arrogant wealthy chiefs; thereafter, the Prophet ﷺ always welcomed Ibn Umm Maktūm warmly and appointed him governor of Madinah during expeditions.
tafsirEn.80:3:
'And What Would Make You Know? Perhaps He Might Purify Himself (Yazzakkā)!' (v.3–4).

📜 Highlights that the true goal of revelation is the purification of receptive hearts.
tafsirEn.80:4:
'Or Be Reminded, and the Reminder Would Benefit Him!'

📜 A single humble heart benefiting from the Quran outweighs the proud leaders who turn away.
tafsirEn.80:5:
'As for He Who Thinks Himself Self-Sufficient (Man Istaghnā)' (v.5–7).

📜 Refers to the wealthy Quraishi chiefs who deemed themselves above needing divine guidance.
tafsirEn.80:6:
'To Him You Give Attention.'

📜 Out of keen desire for their guidance, though they themselves chose rejection.
tafsirEn.80:7:
'And No Blame Is Upon You If He Does Not Purify Himself!'

📜 Relieves the Prophet ﷺ of any burden over those who stubbornly refuse to purify their souls.
tafsirEn.80:8:
Honoring the Humble Seeker Who Comes Running in Reverence (v.8–10).

📜 Praises ‘Abdullāh ibn Umm Maktūm and every student of sacred knowledge who approaches Allāh's Book with eagerness and awe.
tafsirEn.80:9:
'While He Fears Allāh (Wa Huwa Yakhshā)!'

📜 Reverence of Allāh in the heart is the key to benefiting from knowledge.
tafsirEn.80:10:
The Divine Admonition Preserved Forever as Recited Revelation.

📜 Scholars note that the preservation of this gentle admonition at the opening of the surah is one of the clearest proofs of the Prophet's ﷺ absolute truthfulness in conveying every word from his Lord.
tafsirEn.80:11:
The Exalted Honor of the Quranic Scrolls (v.11–16).

📜 Declares that the Quran is a universal Reminder open to whoever wills to remember it, inscribed in honored scrolls.
tafsirEn.80:13:
'In Honored, Exalted, and Purified Scrolls' (v.13–14).

📜 Preserved in the Celestial Tablet (*Al-Lawh al-Mahfūdh*), lofty in rank and purified from every flaw.
tafsirEn.80:15:
'In the Hands of Noble and Dutiful Angelic Scribes (Safarah)' (v.15–16).

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4937 & Muslim #798): The *Safarah* are the noble, righteous angels who convey revelation; the Prophet ﷺ promised that the one who recites the Quran skillfully will be in the company of these noble, dutiful angels!
tafsirEn.80:16:
'Noble and Dutiful (Kirāmin Bararah)!'

📜 Pure in creation and completely obedient to Allāh.
tafsirEn.80:17:
Refuting Human Arrogance by Reminding Man of His Origin (v.17–23).

📜 Asks what makes the disbelieving human so ungrateful when Allāh created him from a humble drop, proportioned him, eased his birth, causes him to die, and will resurrect him.
tafsirEn.80:24:
'Then Let Man Look at His Food!' (v.24–32).

📜 Invites humanity to reflect on how Allāh pours down rain, splits the earth with sprouting seeds, and brings forth grain, grapes, olives, date-palms, and lush gardens as both sustenance and a sign of the Resurrection.
tafsirEn.80:33:
When the Deafening Blast (As-Sākhkhah) Comes on Judgment Day (v.33–37).

📜 Depicts the overwhelming trumpet blast of the Resurrection.
tafsirEn.80:34:
'On the Day a Man Will Flee from His Brother, His Mother, His Father, His Wife, and His Children!' (v.34–36).

📜 So immense is the reckoning that people flee even from those dearest to them in the world.
tafsirEn.80:35:
'And His Mother and His Father.'

📜 Every soul is absorbed in its own account before Allāh.
tafsirEn.80:36:
'And His Wife and His Children.'

📜 Worldly ties cannot substitute for personal faith and deeds.
tafsirEn.80:37:
'For Every Person That Day Will Be a Matter Sufficient to Occupy Him!'

📜 Hadith of ‘Ā'ishah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #6527 & Muslim #2859): When the Prophet ﷺ said that humanity would be gathered barefoot and uncircumcised on Judgment Day and ‘Ā'ishah asked if men and women would look at one another, he recited this verse and said: 'O ‘Ā'ishah, the matter will be far too severe for anyone to look at another!'
tafsirEn.80:38:
The Radiant, Laughing, Rejoicing Faces of the Believers (v.38–42).

📜 Contrasts the bright, joyful faces of the righteous entering Paradise with the dust-covered faces of the wicked.
tafsirEn.97:2:
'And What Can Make You Know What the Night of Decree Is?' (v.2–3).

📜 Magnifies the honor of *Laylat al-Qadr*, the blessed night of Ramadān in which the Quran descended.
tafsirEn.97:3:
'The Night of Decree Is Better Than a Thousand Months!'

📜 Hadith of Abū Hurayrah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #1901 & Muslim #760): Worship and righteous deeds performed during this single night are better with Allāh than worship performed across a thousand months (over 83 years and 4 months); whoever stands in prayer on Laylat al-Qadr out of faith and seeking reward has all his past sins forgiven.
tafsirEn.97:4:
The Descent of the Angels and Jibrīl (Ar-Rūh) by Their Lord's Permission.

📜 The angels and Angel Jibrīl descend in multitudes onto the earth with blessings and divine decrees for the coming year.
tafsirEn.97:5:
'Peace It Is Until the Emergence of Dawn!'

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid & Ash-Sha‘bī: From sunset until the break of dawn, the entire night is pure peace, safety, and angelic greeting for the believers.
tafsirEn.91:8:
'And Inspired It with Its Discernment of Wickedness and Righteousness!'

📜 Hadith of ‘Imrān ibn Husayn (Sahīh Muslim #2650) & Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: After seven majestic cosmic oaths (by the sun, moon, day, night, heaven, earth, and the human soul), Allāh declares that He endowed every soul with the innate capacity to recognize evil and shun it, and to recognize piety and embrace it.
tafsirEn.91:9:
'He Has Succeeded Who Purifies It (Qad Aflaha man Zakkāhā)!'

📜 Supplication of the Prophet ﷺ (Sahīh Muslim #2722): True success belongs to the one who purifies his soul through obedience to Allāh; when reciting this verse, the Prophet ﷺ used to pray: 'O Allāh, grant my soul its piety and purify it; You are the Best to purify it, You are its Guardian and Master!'
tafsirEn.91:10:
'And He Has Failed Who Corrupts It (Wa Qad Khāba man Dassāhā)!'

📜 Whoever buries and stunts his soul in sin, polytheism, and disobedience suffers loss—as illustrated by the tribe of Thamūd at the end of the surah.
tafsirEn.91:11:
The Denial of Thamūd Through Their Transgression (Bi-Taghwāhā).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah: Having stated that whoever corrupts his soul fails (v.10), Allāh cites the tribe of Thamūd who rejected their Prophet Sālih out of collective arrogance and tyranny.
tafsirEn.91:14:
Their Denial and Complete Annihilation (Fa-Damdama ‘Alayhim Rabbuhum).

📜 Because the entire tribe approved of the crime of their most wretched member, Allāh's punishment leveled them all equally after three days.
tafsirEn.91:15:
'And He Does Not Fear the Consequence Thereof (Wa Lā Yakhāfu ‘Uqbāhā)!'

📜 Unlike earthly rulers who fear retaliation, Allāh executes His absolute justice without fearing any consequence.
tafsirEn.85:2:
'And by the Promised Day (Al-Yawm al-Maw‘ūd)!'

📜 Hadith of Abū Hurayrah (At-Tirmidhī #3339) & Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: The Promised Day is the Day of Resurrection, in which Allāh will judge between the persecuted believers and their tyrants.
tafsirEn.85:4:
When and Why Verses 4–9 Were Revealed: The Companions of the Trench (Ashāb al-Ukhdūd).

📜 Hadith of Suhayb Ar-Rūmī (Sahīh Muslim #3005): Revealed to comfort the persecuted believers in Makkah by recounting the story of the believing youth and the believers of Najrān whom a tyrannical king cast into blazing trenches for refusing to abandon monotheism.
tafsirEn.85:11:
The Great Triumph of the Believers in Gardens Beneath Which Rivers Flow.

📜 While the earthly trenches lasted moments, the believers entered eternal Gardens—that is the Supreme Triumph (*Al-Fawz al-Kabīr*).
tafsirEn.85:17:
The Historical Lesson of the Armies of Pharaoh and Thamūd (v.17–20).

📜 Reminds the Makkan polytheists that Pharaoh and Thamūd possessed far greater armies than Quraysh, yet Allāh encompassed them from behind and destroyed them.
tafsirEn.85:22:
'In a Preserved Tablet (Fī Lawhin Mahfūdh)!'

📜 Guarded in the highest heavens from any alteration, addition, or loss.
tafsirEn.95:4:
'We Have Certainly Created Man in the Best of Stature (Ahsani Taqwīm)!'

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: Answering the oaths by the Fig, the Olive, Mount Sinai, and Sacred Makkah, Allāh affirms that He created humanity upright in form, intellect, and spiritual capacity.
tafsirEn.95:7:
'So What Yet Causes You to Deny the Recompense (Ad-Dīn)?'

📜 After seeing how Allāh created you in perfection and transforms you through stages, what excuse remains to deny the Day of Judgment?
tafsirEn.95:8:
'Is Not Allāh the Most Just of Judges (Ahkam al-Hākimīn)?'

📜 Hadith of Abū Hurayrah (Abū Dāwūd #887 & At-Tirmidhī #3347): It is recommended when reciting this final verse to respond: *'Balā, wa anā ‘alā dhālika mina ash-shāhidīn!'* (Yes indeed, and I am among the witnesses to that!).
tafsirEn.106:2:
The Blessing of the Winter Journey to Yemen and Summer Journey to Ash-Shām.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Because Quraysh were the custodians of Allāh's Sacred House (as shown in Surah Al-Fīl), tribes across Arabia respected them, allowing them to travel safely to Yemen in winter and Syria in summer.
tafsirEn.106:4:
'Who Has Fed Them Against Hunger and Made Them Safe from Fear!'

📜 Answering Prophet Ibrāhīm's supplication (Surah 14:37 & 2:126), Allāh granted the people of Makkah both abundant provision and sanctuary from fear.
tafsirEn.101:2:
What Is the Striking Calamity? (v.2–3).

📜 Magnifying the terror of *Al-Qārī‘ah*, one of the names of the Day of Judgment.
tafsirEn.101:4:
'The Day Mankind Will Be Like Scattered Moths (Kal-Farāsh al-Mabthūth)!'

📜 When rising from their graves at the blast of *Al-Qāri‘ah*, people will surge in every direction in bewilderment like moths scattered in the night.
tafsirEn.101:7:
He Shall Be in a Pleasant Life (Rajiyah, v.6–9).

📜 The righteous whose scales are heavy will dwell in supreme bliss.
tafsirEn.101:9:
And His Refuge Will Be Hāwiyah (The Abyss, v.8–11).

📜 Those whose scales are light will tumble into *Hāwiyah*, a blazing fire.
tafsirEn.75:3:
Why Verses 3–4 Were Revealed: Reassembling Man's Bones and Unique Fingertips.

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: Revealed when the Makkan disbeliever ‘Adī ibn Rabī‘ah (or Ubayy ibn Khalaf) asked the Prophet ﷺ if Allāh would really gather crumbling bones on Judgment Day.
tafsirEn.75:16:
When and Why Verses 16–19 Were Revealed: How the Prophet ﷺ Received Revelation.

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #5, #4929 & Sahīh Muslim #448): Ibn ‘Abbās explained that whenever Jibrīl brought revelation, the Prophet ﷺ used to move his tongue and lips rapidly out of eagerness to memorize it; Allāh revealed: *'Move not your tongue with it to hasten it! Indeed, upon Us is its collection in your heart and its recitation!'*
tafsirEn.75:22:
'Faces That Day Will Be Radiant—Looking at Their Lord!' (v.22–23).

📜 Hadith of Suhayb & Jarīr ibn ‘Abdillāh (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #7434 & Sahīh Muslim #181): Proclaims the greatest bliss of the people of Paradise: their faces will shine with beauty and joy as the veil is lifted and they behold the Countenance of their Lord unobstructed, just as they see the full moon on a clear night.
tafsirEn.75:26:
When the Soul Reaches the Collarbones at the Hour of Death (v.26–30).

📜 Depicts the moment of death when the departing soul reaches the throat (*At-Tarāqī*), the family asks *'Who can cure him?'* while the angels ask *'Who will ascend with his soul?'*, and the dying person realizes with certainty that it is the parting from this world.
tafsirEn.75:36:
'Does Man Think That He Will Be Left Neglected (Sudā)?' (v.36–40).

📜 Exegesis of Ash-Shāfi‘ī & Mujāhid: *Sudā* means left without command, prohibition, resurrection, or accountability; He Who created man from a drop and proportioned him is surely able to give life to the dead!
tafsirEn.104:2:
Why Surah Al-Humazah Was Revealed: Hoarding Wealth and Slandering Believers (v.1–3).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: Revealed condemning the arrogant mockers of Quraysh (such as Al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and Al-Walīd ibn Al-Mughīrah) who slandered believers to their faces and behind their backs while hoarding wealth.
tafsirEn.104:4:
'No! He Will Surely Be Thrown into the Crusher (Al-Hutamah)!' (v.4–5).

📜 Just as he sought to crush people's honor with his tongue, he is cast into *Al-Hutamah*, the Fire that crushes everything thrown into it.
tafsirEn.77:7:
'Indeed, What You Are Promised Will Surely Occur!' (v.7–14).

📜 Answering the five opening oaths (by the winds and the angels descending with revelation), Allāh affirms that the Resurrection is an inevitable reality when the stars are extinguished, the sky is cleft, and the mountains are blown away.
tafsirEn.77:15:
'Woe, That Day, to the Deniers!' (Repeated 10 Times in the Surah).

📜 Each cosmic proof of Allāh's power is followed by this solemn warning against denying the Resurrection.
tafsirEn.50:16:
'And We Are Closer to Him Than His Jugular Vein!' (v.16–18).

📜 Allāh's knowledge and guardian angels encompass humanity more intimately than their own jugular vein.
tafsirEn.50:19:
The Trance of Death and the Truth Unveiled (v.19–29).

📜 The reality of the agony of death and the driving angels leading every soul to its final station.
tafsirEn.90:8:
Did We Not Grant Him Two Eyes, a Tongue, and Two Lips? (v.8–10).

📜 Reminding humanity of Allāh's physical gifts and showing them the two contrasting mountain passes of good and evil.
tafsirEn.90:11:
Yet He Has Not Attempted the Steep Path (Al-‘Aqabah, v.11–20).

📜 Explains that the steep path of salvation is freeing a slave, feeding an orphan or needy person in times of hardship, and enjoining patience and mercy.
tafsirEn.86:4:
'There Is No Soul But Has Over It a Protector' (v.4–10).

📜 Every human being is closely guarded by recording angels; reminds man of his humble creation from spurting fluid.
tafsirEn.54:17:
'And We Have Certainly Made the Quran Easy for Remembrance' (Repeated 4 Times).

📜 Allāh guarantees that the Quran is accessible for memorization, recitation, and guidance.
tafsirEn.38:17:
Patience with the Trials of Prophet Dāwūd (David, v.17–20).

📜 Praises Dāwūd's strength, constant turning to Allāh, and the mountains and birds joining him in glorification.
tafsirEn.38:30:
Prophet Sulaymān (Solomon) and His Repentance (v.30–40).

📜 The test of Sulaymān and his profound devotion and turning back to his Lord.
tafsirEn.36:13:
The Parable of the People of the City (Ashāb al-Qaryah, v.13–29).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Qatādah: The mission of the three messengers to Antioch and the martyrdom of Ḥabīb an-Najjār who entered Paradise instantly.
tafsirEn.36:65:
The Day Hands Speak and Feet Bear Witness (v.65).

📜 Human limbs testifying against their owners on Judgment Day.
tafsirEn.25:23:
Turning the Disbelievers' Deeds into Scattered Dust (v.23).

📜 Allāh reducing all worldly deeds done without sincere faith to floating dust particles.
tafsirEn.76:5:
The Righteous Drinking from Cup-Bearers in Paradise (Kāfūr, Salsabīl, v.5–22).

📜 Describing the immense rewards, silken garments, and silver goblets prepared for those who fed the poor out of love for Allāh.
tafsirEn.27:15:
The Wisdom of Dāwūd and Sulaymān & the Ant of the Valley (v.15–44).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Sulaymān's understanding of the ant's speech, the hoopoe bird, and the conversion of the Queen of Sheba (Balqīs).
tafsirEn.91:12:
When the Most Wretched of Them Rushed Forth (Idh Inba‘atha Ashqāhā).

📜 Hadith of ‘Abdullāh ibn Zam‘ah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4942 & Muslim #2855): The Prophet ﷺ explained that a mighty, wicked man among Thamūd (Qudār ibn Sālif) rose with the backing of his whole tribe to hamstring the miraculous She-Camel sent by Allāh.
tafsirEn.91:13:
The Warning of Allāh's Messenger Sālih: 'Leave Allāh's She-Camel and Her Drink!'

📜 Prophet Sālih warned them not to harm the She-Camel of Allāh nor deprive her of her appointed day of water.
tafsirEn.85:3:
'And by the Witness and What Is Witnessed (Wa Shāhidin wa Mashhūd)!'

📜 Hadith of Abū Hurayrah & Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Encompasses Friday (the Witness) and the Day of ‘Arafah (the Witnessed), as well as the Prophets and their nations on Judgment Day.
tafsirEn.85:5:
'Of the Fire Full of Fuel (An-Nār Dhāt al-Waqūd)!'

📜 Trenches dug in the earth and filled with blazing timber to burn the steadfast believers.
tafsirEn.85:6:
'When They Sat by It (Idh Hum ‘Alayhā Qu‘ūd).'

📜 The callous tyrant and his soldiers sat around the edges of the fiery trenches watching the believers burn.
tafsirEn.85:7:
'And They Were Witnesses to What They Were Doing to the Believers!'

📜 Just as they bore witness to their own crime in this world, Allāh Himself is Witness over all things on Judgment Day.
tafsirEn.85:8:
Their Only 'Crime': Believing in Allāh, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy (v.8–9).

📜 The tyrants resented the believers for no fault other than their pure faith in Allāh, to Whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth.
tafsirEn.85:9:
'To Whom Belongs the Dominion of the Heavens and the Earth; and Allāh Is Witness Over All Things!'

📜 Consoles the oppressed: the True Sovereign watches every trial and records every tear and sacrifice.
tafsirEn.85:10:
The Door of Repentance vs. the Torment of Burning for Persecutors.

📜 Comment of Al-Hasan Al-Basrī: Marvel at Allāh's generosity: even after they burned His believing saints, He still called them to repent—while warning those who die unrepentant of the torment of Hell!
tafsirEn.85:12:
'Indeed, the Seizure of Your Lord Is Severe!' (Inna Batsha Rabbika la-Shadīd).

📜 Warns the tyrants of Quraysh that when Allāh seizes the oppressors, His grasp is irresistible.
tafsirEn.85:13:
'Indeed, It Is He Who Originates Creation and Repeats It!'

📜 He Who created humanity the first time has complete power to resurrect them for judgment.
tafsirEn.85:14:
'And He Is the All-Forgiving, the Most Loving (Al-Ghafūr al-Wadūd)!'

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Allāh forgives all who repent and loves His sincere, obedient servants with a pure love that fills the hearts of creation with affection for them.
tafsirEn.85:15:
'Lord of the Glorious Throne (Dhū al-‘Arsh al-Majīd)!'

📜 Sovereign of the Most Exalted Throne.
tafsirEn.85:16:
'Doer of Whatever He Wills (Fa‘‘ālun limā Yurīd)!'

📜 Nothing in the universe can delay or overturn what Allāh decrees.
tafsirEn.85:21:
'Rather, It Is a Glorious Quran!' (Bal Huwa Qur'ānun Majīd).

📜 Noble, exalted, and abounding in wisdom and blessing.
tafsirEn.95:5:
'Then We Returned Him to the Lowest of the Low (Asfala Sāfilīn)!'

📜 Exegesis of Mujāhid, Qatādah & Ibn ‘Abbās: Encompasses both physical decline into extreme old age and spiritual fall into the lowest depths of Hellfire when man corrupts his innate nature through disbelief.
tafsirEn.95:6:
'Except Those Who Believe and Do Righteous Deeds: For Them Is an Unceasing Reward!'

📜 Statement of Ibn ‘Abbās: Whoever preserves his youth in faith and studying the Quran has his reward written in full even when old age weakens him, receiving an eternal reward (*Ajrun Ghayru Mamnūn*).
tafsirEn.106:3:
'So Let Them Worship the Lord of This House (Al-Bayt)!'

📜 Commands Quraysh to worship Allāh alone—the Lord of the Ka‘bah through Whom they enjoyed all their honor—rather than lifeless idols.
tafsirEn.101:5:
'And the Mountains Will Be Like Carded Wool (Kal-‘Ihn al-Manfūsh)!'

📜 The solid mountains of multicolored rock are shattered until they float away like fluffed wool.
tafsirEn.101:6:
The Heavy Scales of Good Deeds (Man Thaqulat Mawāzīnuh, v.6–7).

📜 Whoever has his scale of faith and righteous deeds outweigh his sins enters a life of eternal contentment (*‘Īshatin Rādiyah*) in Paradise.
tafsirEn.101:10:
'And What Can Make You Know What Hāwiyah Is?' (v.8–10).

📜 As for the one whose scale of good deeds is light, his abode into which he plunges headfirst is the Abyss (*Al-Hāwiyah*).
tafsirEn.101:11:
'It Is a Raging, Scorching Fire (Nārun Hāmiyah)!'

📜 Hadith of Abū Hurayrah (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3265 & Muslim #2843): The Prophet ﷺ stated that worldly fire is only one part out of seventy parts of the heat of Hellfire.
tafsirEn.75:4:
'Yes Indeed! We Are Able to Proportion Even His Fingertips (Banānah)!'

📜 Allāh affirms His power not only to reassemble the largest bones, but to restore the finest details of every individual's fingertips.
tafsirEn.75:17:
'Indeed, Upon Us Is Its Collection and Its Recitation (Jam‘ahu wa Qur'ānah)!'

📜 Allāh guaranteed to gather the Quran firmly in the Prophet's ﷺ chest and enable his tongue to recite it perfectly.
tafsirEn.75:18:
'So When We Have Recited It Through Jibrīl, Follow Its Recitation!'

📜 Thereafter, the Prophet ﷺ would listen attentively in silence until Jibrīl finished, and whenever Jibrīl departed, the Prophet ﷺ recited it exactly as Jibrīl had recited it (Al-Bukhārī #5).
tafsirEn.75:19:
'Then Indeed, Upon Us Is Its Explanation (Bayānah)!'

📜 Allāh also guaranteed to explain its lawful and unlawful rulings and deep meanings through the Prophet's ﷺ Sunnah.
tafsirEn.75:23:
'Looking Toward Their Lord (Ilā Rabbihā Nādhirah)!'

📜 Nothing given to the inhabitants of Paradise is more beloved to them than looking upon their Glorious Lord (Sahīh Muslim #181).
tafsirEn.104:3:
'He Thinks That His Wealth Will Make Him Immortal (Akhladah)!'

📜 Deluded by his riches into acting as though he will never die or face judgment.
tafsirEn.104:5:
'And What Can Make You Know What the Crusher Is?'

📜 Magnifies the terror of this level of Hellfire.
tafsirEn.104:6:
'It Is the Fire of Allāh, Eternally Kindled (Al-Mūqadah)!'

📜 A fire kindled by Allāh's wrath that never dies down.
tafsirEn.104:7:
'Which Mounts Directed Straight at the Hearts (Al-Af'idah)!'

📜 Exegesis of Muhammad ibn Ka‘b: Because the heart (*Fu'ād*) was the seat of their arrogance, malice, and disbelief, the fire penetrates straight to their hearts before closing over them in towering columns.
tafsirEn.77:8:
'So When the Stars Are Obliterated (Tumisat)!'

📜 Their light is wiped out on the Day of Decision (*Yawm al-Fasl*).
tafsirEn.77:20:
The Proof of First Creation in the Womb (v.20–24).

📜 Reminds man how Allāh created him from a humble fluid placed in a secure lodging (the womb) for a measured term—proving His absolute power to recreate.
tafsirEn.77:25:
The Earth as a Sanctuary for the Living and the Dead (Kifātā, v.25–28).

📜 Allāh made the earth a receptacle holding the living upon its surface and the dead within its depths, stabilized by lofty mountains and sweet water.
tafsirEn.77:29:
The Three-Columned Shadow of Hellfire (v.29–40).

📜 Contrasts the scorching shadow of smoke on Judgment Day for the deniers with the cool shade and springs prepared for the righteous.
tafsirEn.77:41:
The Righteous Amidst Cool Shade, Springs, and Fruits (v.41–44).

📜 Thus Allāh rewards the doers of good (*Al-Muhsinīn*) with eternal peace and joy.
tafsirEn.77:48:
Why Verse 48 Was Revealed: 'And When It Is Said to Them: Bow in Prayer, They Do Not Bow!'

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Muqātil: Revealed regarding the arrogant tribe of Thaqīf (or the polytheists of Quraysh) who refused out of pride to bow and prostrate to Allāh.
tafsirEn.77:50:
'Then in What Statement After This Quran Will They Believe?'

📜 Hadith of Abū Hurayrah (Abū Dāwūd #887): Closes the surah asking what message could possibly guide a heart that turns away from the clear, miraculous Book of Allāh.
tafsirEn.50:39:
Patience and Glorifying Allāh Before Sunrise and Before Sunset (v.39–40).

📜 Hadith of Jarīr ibn ‘Abdillāh (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #554 & Muslim #633): The Prophet ﷺ looked at the full moon and told his companions that they would see their Lord clearly on Judgment Day, then recited this verse instructing them never to neglect the Fajr prayer before sunrise and the ‘Asr prayer before sunset, along with night prayer.
tafsirEn.86:5:
'So Let Man Observe From What He Was Created!' (v.5–8).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: Invites humanity to reflect on their origin from a humble fluid proceeding from between the backbone and the ribs—proving that He Who originated man is fully able to bring him back (*Raj‘ih*) on Judgment Day.
tafsirEn.86:11:
'By the Sky Which Returns Rain, and the Earth Which Cracks Open with Plants!' (v.11–12).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās & Mujāhid: Swears by the sky that cyclically returns rain season after season and the earth that splits open with green shoots—a living mirror of bodily resurrection.
tafsirEn.86:13:
'Indeed, This Quran Is a Decisive Word—Not Amusement!' (v.13–17).

📜 The Quran separates truth from falsehood (*Qawlun Fasl*) with complete seriousness, while Allāh grants the plotting disbelievers a brief respite.
tafsirEn.54:2:
When They See a Miraculous Sign, They Turn Away Calling It 'Continuous Magic'.

📜 Hadith of Ibn Mas‘ūd (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3869 & Muslim #2800): Even after beholding the moon split in two in the sky above Makkah, the stubborn chiefs of Quraysh followed their desires and claimed Muhammad ﷺ had bewitched their eyes.
tafsirEn.54:9:
The People of Nūh and the Deluge: 'I Am Overpowered, So Help Me!' (v.9–16).

📜 Recounts how the people of Nūh called him mad and rejected him until he supplicated his Lord, whereupon Allāh opened the gates of heaven with pouring water and caused the earth to burst with springs, carrying Nūh upon the Ark built under Allāh's Eyes.
tafsirEn.54:18:
The Destruction of ‘Ād by the Furious Hurricane (v.18–22).

📜 When ‘Ād denied Prophet Hūd, Allāh sent against them a roaring wind on a day of continuous calamity, uprooting men as if they were trunks of uprooted palm trees.
tafsirEn.54:54:
'Indeed, the Righteous Will Be Among Gardens and Rivers—In a Seat of Honor Near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability!' (v.54–55).

📜 Crowns the surah with the eternal abode of truth (*Maq‘adi Sidq*) near the Omnipotent King (*Malīkin Muqtadir*).
tafsirEn.38:41:
The Patience and Supplication of Prophet Ayyūb (Job, v.41–44).

📜 Hadith of Anas ibn Mālik & Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās: After years of severe illness and loss, Prophet Ayyūb called upon his Lord; Allāh commanded him to strike the ground with his foot, bringing forth a cool spring to bathe in and drink from, restoring his health and doubling his family as a mercy and reminder for people of understanding, while praising him: *'Indeed, We found him patient—what an excellent servant!'*
tafsirEn.38:71:
The Creation of Adam and the Arrogance of Iblīs (v.71–85).

📜 Recounts Allāh shaping Adam with His Hands, breathing into him the spirit created by Him, the prostration of all the angels, and the downfall of Iblīs caused by pride (*Istikbār*).
tafsirEn.72:8:
Why the Heavens Were Filled with Stern Guards and Shooting Stars (v.8–10).

📜 Hadith of Ibn ‘Abbās (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #4921 & Muslim #449): The Jinn testified that when the Prophet ﷺ was sent with the Quran, the heavens were guarded with mighty angels and flaming meteors (*Shuhub*) to prevent devils from eavesdropping on the heavenly assembly, preserving the Revelation completely intact.
tafsirEn.72:18:
'And the Mosques Are for Allāh Alone, So Do Not Invoke Anyone Along with Allāh!' (v.18–20).

📜 Exegesis of Sa‘īd ibn Jubayr & Qatādah: Declares that places of worship—and the seven limbs of prostration—belong exclusively to Allāh, commanding pure monotheism.
tafsirEn.36:33:
Cosmic Signs of Resurrection: The Dead Earth Revived, the Night, the Sun, and the Moon (v.33–40).

📜 Hadith of Abū Dharr (Sahīh Al-Bukhārī #3199 & Muslim #159): Points to the revival of barren land with rain and grain, the stripping of daylight from night, and the precise orbits of the sun and the moon—when the Prophet ﷺ asked Abū Dharr where the sun goes at sunset, he explained that it prostrates beneath the Throne of its Lord and asks permission to rise again.
tafsirEn.36:55:
The Joy of the People of Paradise & the Greeting 'Peace!' from a Merciful Lord (v.55–58).

📜 Describes the dwellers of Paradise rejoicing in shade upon raised couches with their spouses, receiving every fruit they desire and the supreme greeting of *'Salām'* (Peace) from their Merciful Lord.
tafsirEn.76:2:
Creating Man from a Mingled Drop to Test Him, Endowing Him with Hearing and Sight (v.2–3).

📜 Allāh created humanity from a mingled drop (*Nutfatin Amshāj*), gave them hearing and sight, and showed them the clear path—whether they choose to be grateful believers (*Shākirā*) or ungrateful deniers (*Kafūrā*).
tafsirEn.76:7:
Fulfilling Vows and Feeding the Needy, the Orphan, and the Captive Purely for Allāh's Face (v.7–10).

📜 Exegesis of Ibn ‘Abbās, Mujāhid & Qatādah: Praises the righteous (*Al-Abrār*) who fulfill their vows of obedience, dread the widespread hardship of Judgment Day, and give their cherished food to the poor, the orphan, and the captive, saying in their hearts: *'We feed you only for the Face of Allāh; we wish from you neither reward nor thanks!'*
tafsirEn.76:11:
Allāh Protecting Them from the Evil of That Day and Granting Them Radiance and Joy (v.11–22).

📜 Because they feared Judgment Day in the world, Allāh shielded them from its terror, brightened their faces with radiance (*Nadrah*), filled their hearts with joy (*Surūr*), and rewarded their patience with Paradise and silk.
tafsirEn.76:23:
'Indeed, It Is We Who Have Sent Down to You the Quran Progessively—So Be Patient!' (v.23–26).

📜 Reassures the Prophet ﷺ that Allāh Himself sent down the Quran stage by stage, commanding him to endure patiently his Lord's decree, refuse obedience to every sinner or disbeliever, and glorify Allāh morning, evening, and through the night.
tafsirEn.67:3:
